title: Cardiovascular effects of continued vs. discontinued anabolic-androgenic steroid use: a longitudinal follow-up study.
abstract: AIMS: Anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) use is prevalent among men engaged in strength training and is associated with adverse structural and functional cardiac changes, but longitudinal data are lacking. This follow-up study examined myocardial effects of AAS with continued use and reversibility following discontinuation. METHODS AND RESULTS: Participants of a previously published cohort (2017-19) of 101 AAS users and 71 non-using weightlifting controls (WLCs) were invited for a follow-up study and underwent interviews, hormonal profiling, and transthoracic echocardiography. Current AAS users at baseline were continued or discontinued users at follow-up, while former users at baseline were those with continued abstinence and those who relapsed.Among those re-enrolled, 70 were AAS users, of whom 35 continued, 15 discontinued, 14 maintained abstinence, and 6 relapsed, and 35 were WLCs. Continued AAS users had persistent indexed left ventricular mass (LVMI 119 ± 30 g/m2), reduced LV ejection fraction (LVEF 48 ± 10%), and worsened diastolic function. Continued AAS users receiving antihypertensive therapy showed improved LVEF compared with untreated users (Δ = 5 ± 8 vs. -4 ± 8%, P = 0.005). Discontinued AAS users showed reduction in LVMI (Δ = -21 g/m2, P = 0.01) and improved LVEF (Δ = 6%, P < 0.001). At follow-up, these changes were comparable with WLCs, which showed statistically but clinically insignificant differences. CONCLUSION: Continued AAS use was associated with sustained LV hypertrophy, LV systolic dysfunction, and worsening diastolic function. Antihypertensive therapy among ongoing AAS users was associated with improved LV systolic function. Discontinuation of AAS use was associated with improvement in cardiac structure and function towards values observed in WLCs.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes following aortic valve replacement: a nationwide observational study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce major adverse cardiovascular events among patients with diabetes, overweight, and obesity. Whether these benefits extend to patients undergoing aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains unknown. Thus, we investigated the association between GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes after AVR. METHODS: Nationwide population-based cohort study including consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI or SAVR in Western Denmark between January, 2016 and April, 2022. Patients were followed until death, emigration, crossover, or end of follow up on May 12, 2026. Propensity score-matching was performed to balance confounding. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or aortic valve reoperation. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, aortic valve reoperation, with analyses accounting for the competing risk of death. RESULTS: Among 5259 eligible patients undergoing AVR, 292 propensity score-matched patients were included in the final analyses. During a mean follow up of 4.8±2.4 years, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.50-0.96, p=0.029). GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was also associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.46-0.95, p=0.025). In competing risk analyses accounting for death, lower risks were observed for heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.67, 95%CI 0.48-0.93, p=0.018), and aortic valve reoperation (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.49-0.98, p=0.037). CONCLUSION: Treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonists was associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes including mortality following AVR among patients with severe AS.

title: Real-Life Psychological Experiences and Cardiac Autonomic Physiology Among Survivors of a Myocardial Infarction in Midlife.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Young and middle-aged women with ischemic heart disease have a higher burden of psychosocial factors compared with male counterparts. They also have worse morbidity and mortality, despite less atherosclerotic burden. Data on daily life stress and autonomic physiology could help guide targeted interventions. METHODS: We studied 302 individuals ≤61 years of age recently hospitalized for a myocardial infarction. All underwent a 7-day home monitoring of mood and stress using ecological momentary assessments, with concomitant Holter monitoring for autonomic physiology. Deceleration capacity, a prognostic marker of parasympathetic activity, was the primary autonomic outcome; heart rate variability was also examined. RESULTS: The sample was 43% women with mean age of 51 years (SD, 7 years). Across the week of monitoring, women reported higher levels of negative mood and stress than men. Women also exhibited significantly lower parasympathetic activity (daily average of deceleration capacity) than men; heart rate variability was also lower. Among women, daily negative mood was inversely associated with lower deceleration capacity: for each 1-log unit higher daily negative mood score, deceleration capacity declined 4.5% in women, but among men, the difference was close to zero: 0.5% (P=0.02 for interaction). Adjustment for other risk factors did not materially affect the associations. A similar pattern of results was observed for heart rate variability metrics. CONCLUSIONS: Young and middle-aged women who recently survived a myocardial infarction have more parasympathetic withdrawal than men in daily life, especially during moments of negative mood. These results underscore the need for greater attention to psychosocial management in women after myocardial infarction.

title: Cellular consequences of non-ablative radiotherapy, a novel approach to ventricular tachycardias.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Radiotherapy (RT) with a single application of ionizing radiation (STAR) has been suggested as a non-invasive alternative to radiofrequency in ablating ventricular tachycardia (VT). Emerging data reveal that STAR may suppress VT without substrate destruction, by enhancing impulse conduction instead, through increased expression of NaV1.5 channels and connexin 43. The study aims to investigate electrophysiology and intracellular Ca2+ dynamics in cardiomyocytes (CMs) from mice subjected to in-vivo RT. The emerging data led us to evaluate biochemical changes potentially linking electrophysiological response to ionizing irradiation. METHODS: CMs isolated 2 weeks after RT with low-dose (15 Gy) or high-dose (25 Gy) were compared to those of sham-treated mice (CTRL). We evaluated: i) the properties of the transient (INaT) and sustained (INasus) components of INa; ii) AP parameters, including the prevalence of Early After-Depolarizations (EADs); iii) intracellular Ca2+ dynamics; iv) CaMKII phosphorylation and v) ROS content. RESULTS: 25 Gy RT i) increased INaT and, to a larger extent, INasus (increased INasus/INaT ratio); ii) increased AP amplitude, +dV/dtMAX and duration (APD) and facilitated EADs; iii) depressed intracellular Ca2+ dynamics. 15 Gy RT had similar but smaller effects (dose-dependency). 25 Gy RT reduced CaMKII phosphorylation but increased cell ROS content, thus providing a mechanism for the late component of INa (INaL) enhancement. CONCLUSIONS: The results support the view that STAR may supress VT by increasing conduction velocity, with APD prolongation providing an additional mechanism. On the other hand, INasus enhancement and Ca2+ handling depression may impair electrical stability and contractility in the irradiated region.

title: Psychological Stress and the Diurnal Patterns of Sodium Excretion and Blood Pressure: Results From the SABRE Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Psychological stress is associated with reduced blood pressure (BP) dipping, but the underlying mechanisms are unclear. This study examined the associations among stress-induced sodium excretion, diurnal sodium excretion, and BP dipping. METHODS: Apparently healthy adult participants underwent a laboratory session during which urinary sodium excretion was measured before and after mental stress tasks. Participants then completed 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring and separate awake and asleep urine collections. The change in urinary sodium excretion rate with stress was defined as the difference in urinary sodium excretion rate before and after stress. The awake-to-asleep ratio of the urinary sodium excretion rate and systolic BP dipping were calculated from the 24-hour urine and BP measurements. RESULTS: In an adjusted model including age, sex, race, ethnicity, body mass index, mean systolic BP, mean diastolic BP, parental history of hypertension, fasting glucose, and 24-hour creatinine clearance, a smaller stress-induced urinary sodium excretion rate was associated with a lower awake-to-asleep ratio of urinary sodium excretion rate (n=180, B=0.2253 [95% CI, 0.0490-0.4016]). In an adjusted model including age, sex, race, ethnicity, body mass index, current smoking, alcohol use, fasting glucose, 24-hour sodium excretion, 24-hour potassium excretion, 24-hour creatinine clearance, and fractional excretion of sodium, a lower awake-to-asleep ratio of the urinary sodium excretion rate was associated with lower systolic BP dipping (n=175, B=1.0127 [95% CI, 0.0599-1.9656]). CONCLUSIONS: A lower stress-induced urinary sodium excretion rate was associated with a worse diurnal pattern of urinary sodium excretion, which was associated with lower systolic BP dipping. REGISTRATION INFORMATION: clinicaltrials.gov. Identifier: NCT03636490.

title: Occlusion-Focused Triage vs Very-High-Risk NSTEMI Criteria: A DIFOCCULT-3 Substudy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The current ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)/NSTEMI framework may not fully identify patients with ACO who present without diagnostic STE. Although immediate invasive management is recommended for patients with very-high-risk NSTEMI features, these criteria are inconsistently applied in clinical practice. The OMI/NOMI framework has been proposed as an alternative strategy. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare the occlusive and nonocclusive myocardial infarction (OMI/NOMI) classification with guideline-defined very-high-risk non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) criteria for the identification of acute coronary occlusion (ACO) in patients without diagnostic STE. METHODS: This was a substudy of the multicenter, cluster-randomized DIFOCCULT-3 (Time for a Diagnostic Paradigm Shift From ST-Elevation/Non-ST-Elevation to Occlusion/Non-Occlusion Myocardial Infarction-3) trial. Consecutive adult patients without diagnostic STE on the admission electrocardiogram were included and managed according to either the conventional STEMI/NSTEMI or the OMI/NOMI approach. Very-high-risk NSTEMI was defined according to current guidelines. Outcomes included immediate invasive management (within 2 hours) and adjudicated ACO. RESULTS: Among 4,398 patients, very-high-risk NSTEMI criteria identified a small proportion of patients and were inconsistently translated into early intervention. The OMI/NOMI approach selected more patients for early invasive management compared with the STEMI/NSTEMI framework (45.4% vs 13.6%; P < 0.001). Adjudicated ACO was identified within 2 hours more frequently under the OMI/NOMI approach (35.1% vs 16.7%; P < 0.001), without reduction in angiographic yield. CONCLUSIONS: An occlusion-focused diagnostic approach was associated with substantially higher rates of immediate invasive management and earlier identification of patients with adjudicated ACO.

title: Association of Air Pollution Exposure and Risk of Incident Atrial Fibrillation: The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Consistent evidence indicates that air pollution negatively impacts cardiovascular health. However, the relationship between air pollution and atrial fibrillation (AF) is unclear, and exposure measurement error has been a significant concern for prior studies. OBJECTIVE: This prospective cohort study aimed to evaluate the association of chronic air pollution exposure and risk of AF. METHODS: We used data from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, a community-based cohort study conducted in 6 U.S. metropolitan areas. Concentrations of 4 pollutants (PM2.5, NO2, NOx, and O3) were assessed from 2000-2018 using hierarchical spatiotemporal models that incorporated cohort-specific monitoring to estimate ambient exposure at participants' residences. In Cox regression models, pollution estimates were represented as time-varying exposures, with 2-year rolling averages updated every 30 days. In our primary model, we adjusted for demographics and health behaviors. RESULTS: Our study included 6618 participants (mean age 62; 53% female). Over 16.5 years median follow-up, we identified 1055 AF events. In our primary model, an interquartile range increment of NO2 (13.5 ppb) was associated with 29% higher risk of AF (hazard ratio 95% CI: 1.00, 1.67). Associations with PM2.5, NOx, and O3 were weaker but also directionally consistent with higher risk. CONCLUSION: We found evidence linking air pollution exposure to risk of incident AF. These results can be used to inform policy and other public health efforts aimed at alleviating the burden of AF, especially given that NO2 exposure estimates (median 17.3 ppb) fell well below the current U.S. Environmental Protection Agency annual standard of 53 ppb.

title: Early Introduction and Prolonged Full-Dose Anakinra Reduce Recurrence Risk After Discontinuation in Recurrent Pericarditis: An International Multicenter Cohort.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Anakinra is effective in recurrent pericarditis, yet optimal treatment duration and strategies for safe drug discontinuation remain uncertain. Identifying predictors of sustained remission after discontinuation is important for clinical management. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 185 consecutive adult patients with corticosteroid-dependent and colchicine-resistant refractory recurrent pericarditis across 16 international referral centers, who permanently discontinued therapy after clinical remission. The primary end point was pericarditis recurrence after drug discontinuation. Univariate and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed to identify demographic, clinical, and therapeutic predictors of postdiscontinuation relapse. RESULTS: Among 185 patients who discontinued anakinra (58.4% women, mean age 50.4±17.8 years, 77% idiopathic cause), treatment was initiated a median of 10 months (interquartile range [IQR], 4.0-19.5) after the first episode and continued at 100 mg/d for a median of 6 months (IQR, 4-12). Over a median follow-up of 7.2 months (IQR, 1.5-23.3) after discontinuation, 68 patients (36.8%) experienced recurrence, with a median time to recurrence of 2.1 months (IQR, 0.7-8.5). Initiation within 12 months from the first pericarditis episode and maintenance of full-dose therapy (100 mg/d) for ≥6 months were independently associated with lower recurrence risk (hazard ratio [HR], 0.33 [95% CI, 0.18-0.66]; P=0.001 and HR, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.23-0.86]; P=0.017; respectively). CONCLUSIONS: Early initiation of anakinra and maintenance of full-dose therapy for at least 6 months are associated with a significantly lower risk of relapse after discontinuation and may inform treatment duration and discontinuation strategies in recurrent pericarditis.

title: Lipoprotein(a) and long-term revascularization burden: a recurrent-event analysis of the UK Biobank.
abstract: AIMS: To investigate whether elevated Lp(a) is independently associated with cumulative coronary, peripheral, and carotid revascularization burden in a primary prevention cohort. METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed 237 729 UK Biobank participants of European ancestry free of ASCVD at baseline, followed for a median of 14.1 years. Lp(a) was analysed using the ESC/EAS 2025 threshold of 105 nmol/L and continuously (per 50 nmol/L increment). The primary outcome was the total number of coronary, peripheral, and carotid revascularization procedures per person. Given the genetically determined, lifelong nature of Lp(a) exposure, to capture the full sequence of procedures over time, rather than time-to-first-event alone, we applied recurrent-event statistical models, including the Andersen-Gill model, negative binomial regression, and the Prentice-Williams-Peterson gap-time model. Overall, 10 731 revascularization procedures occurred in 237 729 participants. The proportion undergoing ≥1 procedure was higher with Lp(a) ≥ 105 vs. <105 nmol/L (4.36% vs. 2.96%), with larger differences for ≥2 (1.53% vs. 0.95%) and ≥3 procedures (0.36% vs. 0.18%). In Andersen-Gill analysis, Lp(a) ≥ 105 nmol/L was associated with a higher revascularization rate (HR 1.50, 1.42-1.60), with a 55% higher rate of revascularization procedures during follow-up by negative binomial regression (IRR 1.55, 1.45-1.65). The association was strongest for the first procedure (HR 1.48, 1.40-1.56), attenuated for the second (HR 1.28, 1.09-1.50), and non-significant for the third (HR 1.23, 0.94-1.62). Findings were consistent across coronary and peripheral territories. CONCLUSION: In this large primary prevention cohort, elevated Lp(a) was independently associated with a higher long-term revascularization burden across multiple vascular territories. The association was robust for coronary, supportive for peripheral, and inconclusive for carotid revascularization owing to limited statistical power. These findings, derived from recurrent-event methodology, provide a more complete quantification of Lp(a)-associated cardiovascular procedural risk than time-to-first-event analyses alone.

title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Incident Cardiovascular Events and Death in Treated Serious Mental Illness, Type 2 Diabetes, and Obesity.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Adults with serious mental illness (SMI), type 2 diabetes, and obesity have elevated cardiovascular risk. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have established cardiometabolic benefits in the general population, but their effects in SMI are unclear. We evaluated whether GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risks of incident myocardial infarction (MI), heart failure (HF), and all-cause death. METHODS: This was a retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study of 218 043 adults with SMI, type 2 diabetes, obesity, and active antipsychotic or antidepressant medications in the TriNetX database (73 health care organizations). Outcomes were incident MI, HF, and all-cause death at 1 and 3 years. The primary exposure was GLP-1RA use versus nonuse; secondary analyses examined semaglutide or tirzepatide. Exploratory analyses evaluated sex, race, and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor use. RESULTS: GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risks of incident MI, HF, and all-cause death. Risk differences at 1 and 3 years were -0.007 and -0.010 for MI, -0.011 and -0.018 for HF, and -0.039 and -0.065 for death (all P<0.001). Semaglutide or tirzepatide use was also associated with lower risks of MI, HF, and death (all P<0.001). Findings were directionally consistent after accounting for sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor use. CONCLUSIONS: Adults with treated SMI, type 2 diabetes, and obesity using GLP-1RAs, particularly semaglutide or tirzepatide, had significantly reduced 1- and 3-year risks of incident MI, HF, and all-cause death versus nonusers. These pooled associations should be interpreted in the context of SMI's clinical heterogeneity and the limitations of administrative case ascertainment.

title: Dual Control of Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Levels by ANGPTL3 and ANGPTL8.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Inactivation of ANGPTL3 (angiopoietin-like protein 3; A3) is a proven therapeutic strategy for lowering plasma lipid levels independently of the low-density lipoprotein receptor, yet the optimal approach to inactivate A3 remains unclear. A3 is proteolytically cleaved and circulates as full-length, N-terminal, and C-terminal fragments. The specific contribution of each form of A3, and of its paralog, ANGPTL8 (angiopoietin-like protein 8; A8), in modulating circulating levels of ApoB (apolipoprotein B)-containing lipoproteins remain poorly defined. Clarifying these relationships will inform next-generation A3-directed therapies. METHODS: We performed liver perfusion studies to directly compare the number and composition of very-low-density lipoprotein particles secreted from mice with and without A3. To amplify effects on cholesterol metabolism, we generated Ldlr-/- mice expressing wild-type A3, full-length A3, or N-terminal A3 fragments, with or without coexpression of A8, and analyzed plasma lipids, circulating A3 and A8 complexes, and intravascular lipase activities. Complementary in vitro assays and structural modeling were used to assess relative endothelial lipase inhibition by A3 alone or in complex with A8. RESULTS: Liver perfusion studies revealed that A3 inactivation does not alter the rates of hepatic secretion of very-low-density lipoprotein in wild-type or Ldlr-/- mice. Inactivation of A8 alone lowered plasma low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels by ≈20%, an effect dependent upon the expression of both endothelial lipase and A3. Maximal inhibition of lipoprotein lipase required coexpression of A8 plus both full-length A3 and N-terminal A3 fragments, indicating that A3 cleavage, in addition to A8 expression, is essential for maximal lipoprotein lipase inhibition. In contrast, A8 expression, but not A3 cleavage, was required for optimal endothelial lipase inhibition. CONCLUSIONS: A8 acts in concert with A3 to differentially modulate lipoprotein lipase- and endothelial lipase-mediated lipolysis, which antagonizes hepatic clearance of newly secreted atherogenic ApoB-containing lipoproteins. This mechanistic framework refines our understanding of A3-targeted lipid lowering and highlights the therapeutic potential of dual A3- plus A8-directed strategies to treat dyslipidemia and prevent atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

title: Underserved communities at risk of heart failure: effectiveness of community-based recruitment strategies and burden of unrecognised cardiovascular disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients from socioeconomically deprived and ethnically diverse backgrounds are under-represented in cardiovascular research. EARLY-HF is a community-based pilot study designed to predict incident HF in primary care. We aimed to assess effectiveness of recruitment strategies for engaging underserved populations and quantify the burden of unrecognised CVD. METHODS: Prospective cohort study enrolling 550 adults aged ≥50 years with two or more cardiometabolic risk factors and no prior diagnosis of HF. Participants were recruited via: (i) targeted identification using electronic health records in eight primary care centres; (ii) digital advertising and targeted social media campaign; (iii) ten community outreach events; (iv) direct referral from family or friends. The baseline study visit included ECG, blood sampling, and imaging. RESULTS: 185 (34%) participants were from the most deprived Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) quintile and 97 (18%) were of non-White ethnicity. Primary care and digital advertising were the most effective recruitment strategies, enrolling 444 (81%) and 68 (12%) participants respectively, while maintaining diverse representation. The social media campaign generated 15,207 advertisement clicks and 1,012 expressions of interest at a cost of £5.93 per sign-up. Community outreach events enrolled 5 (1%) participants and were resource intensive. A substantial burden of previously unrecognised CVD was identified: 125 (23%) participants had clinically actionable cardiac abnormalities, including 46 (9%) with previously unrecognised myocardial infarction, 331 (60%) had uncontrolled blood pressure (≥140/90 mmHg), and 162 (30%) had elevated N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP ≥125 pg/ml). CONCLUSIONS: Primary care-embedded and digital recruitment strategies can effectively engage underserved communities at risk of HF, at scale and at low cost. This population has a very high burden of unrecognised CVD.

title: Bleeding With Asundexian Versus Placebo in Patients With Noncardioembolic Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk TIA: OCEANIC-STROKE Randomized Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: OCEANIC-STROKE (XXX) showed that asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing bleeding in patients with noncardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack. We characterized bleeding categories, sites, and key subgroups. METHODS: In the safety population, 12 254 participants received at least 1 dose of asundexian (n=6124) or placebo (n=6130). Bleeding was categorized by International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis criteria as major, clinically relevant nonmajor (CRNM), or minor. While-on-treatment analyses included events through 2 days after the last dose, with death and permanent discontinuation as competing risks. RESULTS: Major bleeding occurred in 117 (1.9%) participants with asundexian and 107 (1.7%) with placebo (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR], 1.10 [95% CI, 0.85-1.44]; P=0.46). Major or CRNM bleeding occurred in 339 (5.5%) and 307 (5.0%), respectively (csHR, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.96-1.30]; P=0.16), and any bleeding in 763 (12.5%) and 752 (12.3%) (csHR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93-1.13]; P=0.65). Treatment effects for major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups, including planned dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 41 (0.7%) and 36 (0.6%) participants. Any gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 186 (3.0%) and 147 (2.4%) (csHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.03-1.59]), and lower gastrointestinal bleeding in 102 (1.7%) and 59 (1.0%) (csHR, 1.75 [95% CI, 1.27-2.41]), primarily rectal bleeding. Any procedure-related bleeding and any mucosal bleeding did not differ significantly. CONCLUSIONS: Asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing major, major or CRNM, or any bleeding. Lower gastrointestinal bleeding was more frequent with asundexian, whereas treatment effects on major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT05686070.

title: Event-Weighted Desaturation Burden and Cardiovascular Mortality in Sleep Apnoea: Findings from a Large Community-Based Prospective Cohort.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Obstructive sleep apnoea's prognostic value is limited by reliance on the apnoea-hypopnoea index (AHI), which fails to capture physiological heterogeneity of respiratory events. We developed a composite metric, event-weighted desaturation burden (EWDB), integrating weighted respiratory event load, regularity of consecutive inter-event intervals, and cumulative desaturation area. We evaluated its association with cardiovascular mortality and its incremental prognostic value compared with AHI and established hypoxic metrics. METHODS: We analysed 4,904 adults from the Sleep Heart Health Study with baseline polysomnography and adjudicated follow-up. EWDB was derived by combining a respiratory weighted index, a distribution factor based on inter-event interval regularity, and event-linked hypoxic burden (HB). RESULTS: The primary outcome was cardiovascular mortality. Over a median follow-up of approximately 11 years, 341 cardiovascular deaths occurred. In fully adjusted multivariable Cox models, higher EWDB was independently associated with cardiovascular mortality. However, AHI and HB associations were attenuated and lost statistical significance after full adjustment. EWDB (per 1-SD increase) remained robustly associated with cardiovascular mortality, whereas AHI did not. Incorporating EWDB into a comprehensive clinical model provided incremental risk stratification. Similar robust associations were observed for fatal coronary heart disease and incident heart failure. CONCLUSIONS: EWDB was independently associated with cardiovascular mortality and provided incremental prognostic information beyond established clinical and sleep-related factors in this cohort. By integrating respiratory event intensity, cumulative burden, and inter-event interval regularity, EWDB may better characterize cardiovascular stress related to sleep-disordered breathing.

title: A multiview video-text model detects obstructive coronary stenosis and predicts 1-year cardiovascular events from angiography.
abstract: Invasive coronary angiography is the reference standard for diagnosing coronary artery disease, yet assessment is subjective, and existing artificial-intelligence tools typically assess stenosis in individual frames or videos and do not integrate the full multiview angiographic study. Here we show that DeepCORO-CLIP, trained on 203,808 angiographic videos and reports from 28,117 patients, interprets whole multiple-video angiograms at once. It detects obstructive stenoses (≥70%), with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.89 internally and externally, and identifies chronic total occlusion (AUROC = 0.90 to 0.95), intra-coronary thrombus and calcification (AUROC = 0.90 to 0.91). It also predicts 1-year cardiovascular events (AUROC = 0.79, 95% CI of 0.74 to 0.84, versus 0.65 for a model derived using clinical variables) and left ventricular ejection fraction (mean absolute error 7.3% versus 8.8% for a previous model), both achieved using coronary angiography alone. In a blinded review of 365 evaluations across 288 angiograms, its reports were clinically usable in 76% of evaluations versus 88% for cardiologists, with comparable false positives (17% versus 14%, P = 0.38); residual missed stenoses reflected an adjustable threshold rather than an absent signal.

title: Combined Associations of Glycoprotein Acetylation With Lipoprotein (a) and hs-CRP (High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein) on Risk of Cardiovascular Disease in MESA.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Higher plasma glycoprotein acetylation (GlycA) concentrations are associated with an increased risk for incident cardiovascular disease (CVD). We investigated the combined associations of GlycA with lipoprotein (a) (Lp[a]) and hs-CRP (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein) with incident CVD. METHODS: We followed 6676 MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) participants, aged 45 to 84 years, without baseline CVD. Lp(a), GlycA, and hs-CRP were evaluated categorically using standard cut points (Lp[a]: 50 mg/dL; GlycA: 400 μmol/L; hs-CRP: 2 mg/L). We used multivariable-adjusted Cox hazards models to evaluate individual and combined associations of these 3 biomarkers with incident CVD, coronary heart disease, and stroke. RESULTS: Compared with those with low GlycA and low Lp(a) levels, an increase in both incident CVD and coronary heart disease risk was observed for those participants with high levels of either or both of these biomarkers. Risk was highest for those with both high GlycA and high Lp(a) levels (CVD hazard ratio [HR]=1.55 [95% CI: 1.15-2.10) and coronary heart disease (HR=1.92 [95% CI, 1.33-2.77). A similar pattern was not observed for individuals with high levels of both GlycA and hs-CRP. Compared with participants with low levels of GlycA, Lp(a), and hs-CRP, those with high levels of all 3 biomarkers had a 1.98-fold higher CVD risk (95% CI, 1.39-2.82), a 2.23-fold higher coronary heart disease risk (95% CI, 1.45-3.44), and a 2.51-fold higher stroke risk (95% CI, 1.24-5.08). CONCLUSIONS: Routine assessment of GlycA in addition to Lp(a) and hs-CRP may help to identify individuals at particularly increased CVD risk who may benefit from more aggressive preventive therapies.

title: Intracoronary imaging to assess atherosclerosis and to guide percutaneous coronary intervention.
abstract: Intracoronary imaging has become an important tool for the in vivo assessment of coronary atherosclerosis and for guiding percutaneous coronary intervention. By enabling high-resolution visualization of coronary anatomy, these modalities allow for more accurate lesion characterization, precise stent sizing, and optimized procedural strategies. In recent years, multiple randomized controlled trials have demonstrated that imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention reduces major adverse cardiac events (including cardiac death, myocardial infarction, and repeat revascularization), particularly in complex clinical and anatomical settings. This state-of-the-art review synthesizes contemporary evidence supporting the use of intravascular ultrasound and optical coherence tomography to guide percutaneous coronary intervention and improve clinical outcomes, drawing from recent trial data and current guideline recommendations. Special emphasis is placed on complex lesion subsets, such as left main coronary artery disease and other complex bifurcation lesions, calcified lesions, long lesions, and scenarios involving patients at heightened risk, such as those with acute coronary syndrome. Finally, this review considers the strengths and limitations of intracoronary imaging, as well as unresolved questions and priority areas for future research aimed at further improving patient outcomes.

title: Residual Cardiovascular Risk Beyond Coronary Physiology: Complementary Prognostic Value of Trimethylamine N-Oxide in Patients Undergoing Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography With Computed Tomography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography with CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) enables noninvasive identification of flow-limiting coronary stenosis and is widely used for risk assessment. However, adverse cardiovascular events still occur in a subset of patients without functionally significant ischemia, suggesting that physiological assessment alone may not fully capture patient-level risk. We aimed to evaluate whether circulating trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a gut microbiota-derived biomarker, provides complementary prognostic information. METHODS: In this biobank-linked retrospective cohort study, 3978 patients undergoing clinically indicated coronary CT angiography with CT-FFR assessment were included. Serum TMAO concentrations were measured from cryopreserved samples obtained within ±30 days of imaging. Patients were stratified into high and low TMAO groups according to the receiver operating characteristic-derived threshold. The primary end point was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events during a median follow-up of ∼3 years. Multivariable Cox models evaluated associations between TMAO and outcomes, and incremental prognostic value beyond clinical variables and CT-FFR was assessed. RESULTS: Event rates were similar across physiological strata (10.6% for CT-FFR ≤0.80 versus 10.0% for CT-FFR >0.80), indicating outcome heterogeneity beyond ischemia status. Higher TMAO levels were independently associated with major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events after adjustment for clinical covariates and CT-FFR (hazard ratio, 1.82 [95% CI, 1.44-2.31]; P<0.001). Addition of TMAO improved discrimination after bootstrap optimism correction (C-index 0.552-0.591). Among patients with preserved CT-FFR, elevated TMAO identified a subgroup with higher event rates, whereas patients with preserved CT-FFR and low TMAO had the most favorable prognosis. CONCLUSIONS: Physiological assessment and clinical outcomes are not synonymous in patients undergoing coronary CT angiography. Circulating TMAO provides complementary prognostic information and refines risk stratification, particularly among individuals without functionally significant ischemia. Integrating systemic biomarkers with coronary physiological assessment may improve individualized risk evaluation beyond imaging alone.

title: Calprotectin Accelerates Pathogenic Calciprotein Particle Maturation to Promote Vascular Calcification in Chronic Kidney Disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vascular calcification is a hallmark of chronic kidney disease (CKD)-mineral and bone disorder and a major determinant of cardiovascular mortality. Secondary calciprotein particles (CPP2) are key mediators of vascular calcification; however, the mechanisms regulating their maturation and pathogenic properties remain incompletely understood. CPT (Calprotectin, S100A8/A9), a myeloid-derived inflammatory mediator, is elevated in CKD and predicts cardiovascular events and mortality, particularly under high-phosphate conditions, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. METHODS: We investigated the role of CPT in vascular calcification using CKD-mineral and bone disorder mice with myeloid-specific CPT deletion. Aortic calcification was assessed by ex vivo imaging, histology, and calcium quantification. Serum calciprotein particle (CPP) fractions were determined by flow cytometry. Mechanistic studies were performed in vascular smooth muscle cells exposed to CPP2 in the presence or absence of macrophage-derived CPT. Calcification propensity was evaluated using the T50 assay, and CPP2 elemental composition was analyzed by high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy-energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy. RESULTS: Myeloid-specific CPT deletion significantly attenuated aortic calcification and osteogenic gene expression in CKD-mineral and bone disorder mice without altering renal function or systemic mineral parameters. These changes were accompanied by an increased circulating immature CPP fraction. Macrophage-derived CPT markedly enhanced CPP2-induced vascular smooth muscle cell calcification by accelerating CPP maturation, reflected by a shortened T50, and by altering CPP2 composition to be enriched in calcium and phosphate. Although no direct interaction between CPT and CPPs was detected, CPT modified the physicochemical milieu, including ionized calcium and pH. Consistently, CPP2 from CPT-deficient serum exhibited substantially reduced calcification potency, indicating that CPT shapes CPP pathogenicity by modulating particle quality rather than quantity. Importantly, CPT-mediated CPP maturation occurred in a cell-free milieu, indicating a TLR4-independent mechanism distinct from its known receptor-mediated actions. CONCLUSIONS: CPT is a previously unrecognized regulator of pathogenic CPP maturation and composition, thereby promoting vascular calcification in CKD-mineral and bone disorder. Targeting CPT may represent a novel therapeutic strategy to attenuate vascular calcification in CKD.

title: The Impact of Statin Therapy on Postoperative Short- and Long-term Mortality and Morbidity After Non-Cardiac Surgery.
abstract: AIMS: Statins' anti-inflammatory and endothelial-stabilising effects suggest perioperative value, but trials of de novo initiation were discredited following research misconduct. Whether established preoperative statin therapy lowers postoperative mortality dose-dependently remains unclear. METHODS: We studied 56,362 patients aged ≥45 years undergoing non-cardiac surgery at two university hospitals (2016-2023). Preoperative statin exposure was assessed as status (any vs none), intensity (high vs low/intermediate), and regimen (high vs low/intermediate vs none). Primary outcomes were 30- and 365-day mortality. Inverse probability of treatment weighting, using random forest-estimated propensity scores targeting the average treatment effect in the treated, was applied to balance measured confounders. Associations were estimated with weighted Cox regression. RESULTS: Overall, 372 patients (0.6%) died within 30 days and 3,735 (6.6%) within 365 days. After weighting, all covariates were balanced. Statin therapy showed a directionally consistent but non-significant association with lower 30-day mortality (HR 0.78; 95% CI 0.57-1.07), and was associated with lower 365-day mortality (HR 0.81; 95% CI 0.73-0.90; ARD -1.2 percentage points; number needed to treat 83). A dose-response relationship was evident: versus no statin, high-intensity therapy showed a 29% lower hazard (HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.60-0.83; ARD -2.3 points) and low/intermediate-intensity a 16% lower hazard (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.74-0.96). Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSIONS: Among adults undergoing non-cardiac surgery, established preoperative statin therapy was associated with dose-dependent lower 365-day mortality. These findings suggest perioperative statin continuation as a preventive strategy and warrant confirmation in a randomised trial.

title: Impact of prolonged balloon inflation on valve expansion and early clinical outcomes following contemporary balloon-expandable transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Incomplete expansion of balloon-expandable (BE) transcatheter heart valves (THVs) after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) may affect valve performance and durability. Routine THV post-dilatation (the "double-tap" technique) has been proposed to optimise device expansion; however, it may increase procedural complexity. AIMS: We sought to evaluate the impact of a prolonged balloon inflation implantation strategy on BE THV expansion, haemodynamic performance, and early clinical outcomes. METHODS: This single-centre study analysed consecutive TAVI patients treated for native tricuspid aortic stenosis with the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA THV using a prolonged balloon inflation strategy (8 seconds). Valve expansion was assessed by fluoroscopy at multiple frame levels and compared with three validated reference standards. Results were also descriptively compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique. Clinical and haemodynamic outcomes at 30 days were adjudicated according to Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria. RESULTS: A total of 84 patients (mean age 78.8 years, 58% male, median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score 3.9%) were included. Prolonged inflation resulted in complete THV expansion at the inflow and outflow levels, with only mild underexpansion (98.5±1.3%) detected at the midframe level when manufacturer-defined nominal values were used as the reference. When compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique, expansion values for the 23, 26, and 29 mm valves were consistently similar or higher, whereas lower expansion was observed for the 20 mm size. Device success was achieved in all cases, with no stroke at 30 days. Permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 6% of patients. Haemodynamic performance was favourable (mean gradient 9.2 [interquartile range 7.0-10.3] mmHg at 30 days), with no patients having moderate or severe paravalvular leak. CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged balloon inflation during BE THV deployment is associated with favourable valve expansion, haemodynamic results, and a favourable safety profile, consistent with values reported in double-tap series. If confirmed in larger studies, this strategy may represent a simple alternative to routine double-tap in selected patients.

title: Anticoagulation strategies during peripheral ultrafiltration in diuretic-resistant congestive heart failure.
abstract: Introduction and objectives Peripheral ultrafiltration (UF) is an effective strategy for the management of diuretic-resistant congestion in patients with decompensated heart failure. However, extracorporeal circuit clotting remains one of the main technical limitations of the procedure, and the optimal anticoagulation strategy during UF has not been clearly established. The primary aim of this study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of different anticoagulation strategies during UF. Methods This prospective, nonrandomized, single-center study included 87 consecutive patients who underwent UF between January 2021 and November 2025. The anticoagulation strategy was tailored according to the patients' baseline anticoagulant therapy: unfractionated heparin (UFH), n = 8; low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH), n = 41; vitamin K antagonists (VKAs), n = 12; and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), n = 26. Procedural efficacy was defined as successful completion of the UF session without premature interruption due to extracorporeal circuit dysfunction or clinical complications. Results Baseline characteristics and UF technical parameters were comparable among groups (P > .1). Procedural efficacy was highest with intravenous heparin (UFH = 100%, LMWH = 48.7%, VKAs = 66.6%, and DOACs = 65.4%; P = .048). Extracorporeal circuit clotting was more frequent with subcutaneous heparin (UFH = 0%, LMWH = 31.7%, VKAs = 25%, and DOACs = 27%; P = .018). Conclusions UFH was associated with a lower rate of extracorporeal circuit clotting and a higher rate of successful UF completion. Complications were infrequent. Given the observational design and the small sample size, these findings warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies. Full English text available from: www.revespcardiol.org/en.

title: Aldosterone-Producing Lesions Harboring ATP1A1 and ATP2B3 Mutations: An International Multicenter Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Somatic aldosterone-driver mutations are identified in >90% of patients with primary aldosteronism undergoing adrenalectomy, and they display distinct demographic clustering. ATP1A1 and ATP2B3 mutations, encoding the Na+/K+ ATPase α1 subunit and the Ca2+ ATPase 3, respectively, are relatively rare and are often grouped as ATPase mutations. Differences in their clinical and biochemical phenotypes remain understudied. METHODS: This international collaboration of 16 centers included patients with primary aldosteronism harboring pathogenic variants in ATP1A1 and ATP2B3. Clinical data were collected from medical records. Where available, we compared histopathologic features and steroid profiles (from peripheral and adrenal vein samples) by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. RESULTS: We included 300 patients (mean age, 57±11 years; 85% men) with aldosterone-producing lesions harboring ATP1A1 (204) and ATP2B3 (96) mutations. Age and sex distributions were similar. ATP2B3 mutations were associated with lower serum potassium, higher lateralization indices, and stronger contralateral suppression. Postoperative biochemical cure was achieved in 96% of patients with ATP2B3 mutations versus 83% of those with ATP1A1 mutations (P=0.02). Multiple CYP11B2-positive lesions were observed in 47% of ATP1A1 versus 27% of ATP2B3 cases (P=0.03). Baseline peripheral steroid profiling was available in 126 patients (84 with ATP1A1 and 42 with ATP2B3) and showed higher aldosterone concentrations in the ATP2B3 group (median [interquartile range], 31 ng/dL [20-43] versus 23 ng/dL [11-38]; P=0.03). CONCLUSIONS: ATPase mutations are most common in middle-aged men with lateralized primary aldosteronism. Compared with ATP1A1, ATP2B3 mutations are associated with a more severe primary aldosteronism phenotype, stronger lateralization, and higher rates of single aldosterone-producing lesions and postoperative biochemical cure.

title: Real-world, digital-first delivery of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in women.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated substantial weight reduction and cardiometabolic benefit in randomized trials; however, prospective implementation evidence from digital care models and female sex community populations remains limited. Here we report outcomes from an observational study of 8,127 women initiating GLP-1RA therapy (99.8% tirzepatide) through a structured digital program incorporating mandatory biochemical monitoring, weekly video-supported follow-up and clinician-guided dose titration in the UK. Mean weight reduction was 16.1 kg (95% confidence interval 15.9 to 16.2; P < 0.001), representing 15.5% of baseline weight; 83.1% achieved ≥10% and 22.4% achieved ≥20% weight loss, with consistent responses across age, baseline weight and socioeconomic strata. Among participants with paired biomarker data, mean glycated hemoglobin decreased by 3.3 mmol mol-1 (95% confidence interval 3.1 to 3.4; P < 0.001), normalizing in 84.5% of those with baseline diabetes-range values and 96.3% with prediabetes, and lipid parameters improved significantly (reductions in total cholesterol of 0.77 mmol l-1, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol of 0.61 mmol l-1 and triglycerides of 0.47 mmol l-1). Retention was 91.4% at 6 months, with no serious treatment-related adverse events. These findings support the feasibility of delivering structured, digitally enabled obesity pharmacotherapy at scale and provide prospective real-world implementation evidence for this care model. Interpretation is limited by the observational design, absence of a comparator group, self-pay population and 6-month follow-up.

title: Optimizing Echocardiographic Evaluation of Chronic Mitral Regurgitation: Comparison With Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Implications for Guideline Recommendations.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The ASE (American Society of Echocardiography) guidelines recommend the presence of at least 4 specific criteria to confirm a diagnosis of definite severe mitral regurgitation (MR). However, the performance of these criteria, particularly when <4 are present, remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate and optimize the ASE native MR guidelines by comparing them with quantitative cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), considered the reference standard for MR assessment. METHODS: In this prospective study, 177 patients underwent near-simultaneous CMR and transthoracic echocardiography for the assessment of MR. MR severity was classified using a 4-grade scale based on CMR-derived regurgitant volume, which was calculated as the difference between total left ventricular (LV) stroke volume and aortic forward flow. MR severity was similarly graded using the ASE algorithm, with quantification performed when necessary, by averaging the regurgitant volume from 3 methods: 1) the proximal isovelocity surface area method; 2) the biplane LV volumetric method; and 3) the mitral valve volumetric method. RESULTS: The study cohort had a median age of 61.7 years, with 55% being men. Primary MR was the predominant pathology (73% of patients), with 42% having mitral valve prolapse and 25% presenting with flail leaflets. There was exact agreement between transthoracic echocardiography and CMR MR grading in 51% of cases, whereas agreement within 1 grade was observed in 89%. Patients who met any of the ASE severe MR criteria were predominantly classified as having grades 3 to 4 MR by CMR. The following ASE parameters demonstrated high specificity for identifying grade 4 MR by CMR: pulmonary vein systolic flow reversal (specificity 88%), enlarged LV with normal systolic function (specificity 85%), proximal isovelocity surface area radius ≥1.0 cm (specificity 83%), and vena contracta width ≥0.7 cm (specificity 80%). Combining color Doppler with either pulmonary vein systolic reversal or enlarged LV with normal function resulted in 91%-95% specificity for severe MR. Importantly, reliance on fewer ASE criteria reduced the need for quantification from 86% (4 criteria) to 73% (3 criteria) and 59% (2 criteria), thereby enhancing diagnostic efficiency. CONCLUSIONS: Certain ASE criteria, especially when used in combination, are highly specific for diagnosing severe MR, even when <4 criteria are present. This study suggests that in many cases, the reliance on extensive quantification may be reduced, streamlining the diagnostic process and improving clinical workflow.

title: Definition and Prognosis of Mitral Regurgitation in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A Multicenter International Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, mitral regurgitation (MR) severity may be underestimated by conventional (semi-)quantitative echocardiographic criteria due to restrictive low-flow hemodynamics. We sought to define and validate disease-specific MR risk thresholds and compare their prognostic performance with guideline definitions. METHODS: In a multicenter cohort study (8 centers, 4 countries), 1101 patients with newly diagnosed transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (derivation, n=722; validation, n=379) underwent standardized echocardiography with blinded core laboratory analysis, including MR measures (vena contracta width, effective regurgitant orifice area, regurgitant volume, and regurgitant fraction). All-cause mortality and time to first heart failure hospitalization (HFH) served as end points. Prognostic thresholds were derived from spline analysis, validated externally, and compared with American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology, European Society of Cardiology/European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery, and American Society of Echocardiography definitions. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 24.9 months (interquartile range, 12.0-42.0), 314 patients (28.5%) died and 244 (22.2%) experienced HFH. All MR metrics independently predicted mortality and HFH (all P<0.05). Spline-derived thresholds identified intermediate risk at vena contracta width ≥3.0 mm, effective regurgitant orifice area ≥0.10 cm2, regurgitant volume ≥15 mL, and regurgitant fraction ≥20% and high risk at effective regurgitant orifice area >0.25 cm2, regurgitant volume >38 mL, and regurgitant fraction >35%. Compared with guideline grading (≈12%-13%), the composite MR grading scheme classified a significantly higher proportion (21%) as severe MR and provided superior discrimination for clinical outcomes at 12 and 24 months in both the derivation and validation cohort. After multivariable adjustment, only the composite MR grading scheme remained strongly predictive for both mortality (hazard ratio, 1.20 [1.07-1.36]) and HFH (hazard ratio, 1.21 [1.05-1.38]). CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative MR thresholds in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy are substantially lower than current guideline cutoffs. A validated, risk-based composite MR grading scheme improves prediction of both mortality and HFH, better reflecting the restrictive low-flow pathophysiology of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy and supporting disease-specific MR grading. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06836011.

title: Associations of Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2 Activity With Markers of Endothelial Dysfunction and Oxidative Stress in Young Healthy Adults: The African-PREDICT Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone-system plays a major role in the pathogenesis of cardiovascular disease through, among others, endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress. Circulating ACE2 (angiotensin-converting enzyme 2) is emerging as a biomarker of cardiovascular disease risk; however, its role in younger populations is not well-established. This study aimed to investigate sex differences in serum ACE2 activity and associations with endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress-related markers in young, apparently healthy men and women. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, we included 1134 young (aged 20-30 years) men (n=557) and women (n=577). Serum ACE2 activity was measured using a validated fluorometric assay. We analyzed markers of endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and antioxidant capacity. We performed a 2-sample t test and Mann-Whitney U test. We applied multivariable-adjusted Tobit regression analysis to account for left truncation. RESULTS: Men had higher ACE2 activity than women (P<0.001). After multiple adjustments for covariates, ACE2 activity was positively associated with von Willebrand factor (P=0.006), and a disintegrin-like metalloproteinase with thrombospondin motif type 1 member 13 (P=0.019) in men. Among women, ACE2 activity was negatively associated with asymmetric dimethylarginine (P=0.043) and superoxide dismutase (P=0.004). CONCLUSIONS: Serum ACE2 activity was higher in men than women and showed sex-specific associations with endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress-related markers. Our results suggest an association between ACE2 shedding and pathophysiological processes associated with alterations in endothelial integrity and early endothelial dysfunction, which may be influenced by sex. This highlights the role of circulating ACE2 as a potential early biomarker of cardiovascular disease risk in young adults. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03292094.

title: Multivariate Genomic Analysis Reveals Shared Genetic Architecture and Potential Therapeutic Targets for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is a leading cause of mortality worldwide and comprises multiple clinical phenotypes, but their shared genetic architecture remains incompletely defined. METHODS: We integrated genome-wide association study summary statistics for coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, large-artery atherosclerotic stroke, and carotid plaque using genomic structural equation modeling to derive a multivariable ASCVD common factor. We applied fine-mapping, multi-marker analysis of genomic annotation, transcriptome-wide association studies, Mendelian randomization, colocalization, mediation analysis, and virtual screening. RESULTS: We identified 289 linkage disequilibrium-independent lead single-nucleotide polymorphisms mapping to 177 genomic risk loci; 13 lacked corresponding genome-wide significant signals in the input genome-wide association studies. Eleven had prior genome-wide association study catalog association records, whereas no relevant records were identified for the loci represented by rs2294777 near SASH1 and rs4843053 near AKAP13. Fine-mapping prioritized 26 putative causal variants. Integrated functional summary-based imputation, multi-tissue transcriptome-wide association study, and multi-marker analysis of genomic annotation analyses implicated 123 genes. Enrichment analyses highlighted endothelial cells and H3K27ac-marked regulatory regions. Lipidomic analyses linked higher triacylglycerols and sterol esters to increased multivariable ASCVD common factor risk. Protein Mendelian randomization analyses in deCODE and Fenland prioritized aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2), phosphodiesterase 5A (PDE5A), HtrAserinepeptidase 1 (HTRA1), and transcription elongation factor A2 (TCEA2) as candidate targets. Colocalization supported a shared causal variant between TCEA2 and multivariable ASCVD common factor. Mediation analyses suggested partial mediation by diastolic blood pressure for ALDH2, PDE5A, and TCEA2 and by triglycerides for TCEA2. Virtual screening identified candidate compounds with favorable predicted binding to PDE5A and ALDH2. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating multivariate genome-wide association study with multi-omics and causal inference analyses identified shared genetic signals associated with ASCVD susceptibility and prioritized candidate protein targets, informing future functional studies and target validation.

title: Effect of Vasopressin Initiation Threshold on Septic Shock Mortality: The VASSPR Cluster Crossover Randomized Strategy Trial.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: The optimal vasopressor dose at which to initiate a second vasopressor in patients with septic shock is uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of hospital-level strategies initiating vasopressin infusion at a lower threshold vs a higher threshold on outcomes in patients with septic shock. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Cluster-randomized, cluster-crossover, pragmatic clinical strategy trial including adult patients receiving vasopressors for septic shock at 13 hospitals in Idaho and Utah from February 1, 2024, to July 31, 2025. The last day of follow-up for the primary outcome was February 17, 2026. INTERVENTION: Hospital-level implementation of septic shock management strategies recommending fixed-dose vasopressin initiation when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.1 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (lower-threshold strategy) or when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.4 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (higher-threshold strategy). Hospitals were randomized for the first month to an initial strategy (6 hospitals to the lower threshold vs 7 hospitals to the higher threshold) and then crossed over to the alternate strategy monthly thereafter. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome of 28-day mortality and the key secondary outcome of kidney replacement therapy-free days through day 28 were analyzed using multivariable generalized linear mixed-effects models, accounting for trial site and baseline patient characteristics. RESULTS: There were 3959 unique patients with septic shock (median age, 68 [IQR, 57 to 77] years; 1903 [48%] were female). Of the patients more likely to experience differential management under the tested hospital-level vasopressin dose strategies (maximum vasopressor dose ≥0.07 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent), 1034 of 1521 (68.0%) cared for under the lower-threshold strategy received vasopressin compared with 651 of 1526 (42.7%) cared for under the higher-threshold strategy. In the hospital-level strategy recommending a lower-dose threshold for vasopressin initiation, the maximum vasopressor dose received prior to vasopressin initiation was a median of 0.14 (IQR, 0.10 to 0.22) µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent vs 0.34 (IQR, 0.16 to 0.42) µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent in the hospital-level strategy recommending a higher-dose threshold for vasopressin initiation. Mortality at 28 days occurred in 628 of 1975 patients (31.8%) treated with the hospital-level strategy recommending initiation of vasopressin at a lower-dose threshold of other vasopressors vs 655 of 1984 patients (33.0%) treated with the higher-threshold strategy (adjusted marginal odds ratio, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.87 to 1.06], P = .62; adjusted risk difference, -0.4 [95% CI, -2.7 to 1.3] percentage points). Patients in both strategies for vasopressin initiation had a median of 29 (IQR, -1 to 29) kidney replacement therapy-free days (adjusted marginal odds ratio, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.91 to 1.14]). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this large, pragmatic clinical trial comparing the effectiveness of 2 hospital-level strategies for second-line vasopressor management in septic shock, a strategy recommending initiation of vasopressin at a lower dose of other vasopressors did not reduce 28-day mortality compared with a strategy recommending vasopressin initiation at a higher dose of other vasopressors. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06217562.

title: Comparison of Unfractionated Heparin and Low-Molecular-Weight Heparin in Acute Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Subanalysis of the CLOT-VENUS Registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Optimal anticoagulation in acute cerebral vein thrombosis remains uncertain. We compared unfractionated heparin (UFH) and enoxaparin, and identified predictors of functional recovery and UFH responsiveness. METHODS: This retrospective 2-center study from the multicenter international CLOT-VENUS (Collaboration on Cerebral Venous Thrombosis) registry included adults with acute cerebral vein thrombosis treated with UFH or enoxaparin (2004-2024). Baseline clinical, laboratory, and imaging data were collected. UFH response was measured via a composite responsiveness index (Unfractionated Heparin Composite Response Index) based on partial thromboplastin time. The primary outcome was 6-month functional status (modified Rankin Scale [mRS]), and secondary outcomes included discharge mRS and death. RESULTS: Among 359 patients (median age, 40 [interquartile range, 28-54] years; 68.5% women), 220 (61.3%) received UFH and 139 (38.7%) enoxaparin. Only 64% of partial thromboplastin time values fell within the therapeutic range. UFH was associated with worse outcomes at discharge (mRS score, 3-6: adjusted odds ratio, 2.89; mRS score, 2-6: adjusted odds ratio, 1.90; ordinal mRS score, adjusted odds ratio, 1.56) and at 6 months (mRS score, 3-6: adjusted odds ratio, 2.63). Poor recovery was independently linked to the UFH composite responsiveness index and frequent infusion adjustments. Notably, in the sensitivity analysis limited to patients on UFH with ≥50%, ≥67%, and ≥79% therapeutic partial thromboplastin time values, the outcome differences diminished. Age was independently associated with UFH responsiveness, and female sex, body mass index, and NLR with the number of UFH infusion-rate adjustments. CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with UFH was associated with worse clinical outcomes compared with enoxaparin, largely attributable to suboptimal and inconsistent anticoagulation. However, when UFH achieves consistent therapeutic levels, the outcomes are comparable. Early predictors may help guide individualized anticoagulation strategies.

title: Impact of the Extent, Pattern, and Location of Replacement Myocardial Fibrosis on Clinical Outcomes in Aortic Regurgitation.
abstract: AIMS: The prognostic significance of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)-detected replacement myocardial fibrosis in aortic regurgitation (AR) remains incompletely understood. This study aims to explore the association between the extent, pattern, and location of LGE and clinical outcomes in patients with chronic AR. METHODS AND RESULTS: Between 2010 and 2024, consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe AR and no significant coronary artery stenosis who underwent contrast-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) were included. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular mortality, heart transplantation, or rehospitalization for heart failure. The association between LGE characteristics and MACE was evaluated. Overall, 363 patients (mean age 52.6 ± 14.2 years; 54 female) were included. Over a median follow-up of 56.6 months, 73 patients experienced MACE. LGE was present in 200 patients (55.1%). An LGE extent threshold of 2.6% provided robust risk stratification, yielding the highest C-index of 0.797, a likelihood ratio chi-square of 97.30, and the lowest Akaike information criterion of 681.06. Furthermore, predominant subendocardial-involved LGE was present in 13.5% of LGE-positive patients and was independently associated with MACE after adjusting for LGE extent (HR 3.028; 95% CI 1.216-7.539; P = 0.017). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated that patients with both LGE extent >2.6% and predominant subendocardial-involved LGE pattern were at the highest risk of MACE. CONCLUSIONS: In AR, an LGE extent > 2.6% predicts MACE better than LGE presence alone. Furthermore, non-ischemic predominant subendocardial-involved LGE is independently associated with MACE. The coexistence of both features further amplifies the risk of MACE.

title: Deep learning-enabled assessment of right ventricular size and function is associated with cardiovascular outcomes.
abstract: Right ventricular (RV) size and function inform prognosis in many cardiovascular diseases, but assessment by two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography is challenging. Here we show that a deep learning model, Dimensional Reconstruction of Imaging Data-Right Ventricle (DROID-RV), can estimate RV end-diastolic diameter and identify RV systolic dysfunction from transthoracic echocardiography videos. We trained DROID-RV in 17,141 ambulatory cardiology patients (51,188 studies and 383,881 video clips) and validated model predictions in 9,112 primary care patients and 831 patients with RV ejection fraction assessed by three-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography. Across multiple test samples, DROID-RV accurately estimates RV end-diastolic diameter and identifies RV dysfunction, although model prediction error increases at extremes of RV size and function. We additionally show that RV size and function predictions are associated with incident mortality, atrial fibrillation and heart failure. Our work demonstrates how deep learning can automate RV assessment and risk stratification at scale using two-dimensional echocardiography.

title: Algorithmic Guardrails for Echocardiography AI: Deep Feature Representations for Error Slicing and Selective LVEF Estimation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Automated echocardiography analysis using artificial intelligence (AI) currently lacks effective guardrails or oversight mechanisms to ensure its safe and reliable deployment. OBJECTIVES: This study investigated whether deep feature representations can identify echocardiograms at risk of misinterpretation by echocardiography AI-based left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) estimation models. METHODS: We retrospectively validated 2 state-of-the-art models for LVEF estimation, EchoNet (single-task model) and PanEcho (multitask foundation model), on 4,010 apical-4-chamber videos from 1,353 studies (n = 1,208) with biplane LVEF measurements in the MIMIC-IV-ECHO database (2017-2019). We extracted 4 deep feature representations from a view classifier, a left ventricle segmentation model, and the 2 validated LVEF estimation models. These features were evaluated for their ability to identify systematic misinterpretations (error slicing) and automatically exclude AI estimates for high-risk inputs (selective estimation). RESULTS: While PanEcho performed better relative to EchoNet (EchoNet minus PanEcho [Δ], Δmean absolute error: 0.31 [0.07, 0.55]; ΔR2: -0.07 [-0.11, -0.03]), both models systematically overestimated LVEF at lower values (proportional bias slope, EchoNet: -0.33 [-0.39, -0.28], P < 0.001, PanEcho: -0.31 [-0.36, -0.26], P < 0.001). All investigated deep feature representations identified error slices for both models. Shared error slices between the models revealed 2 common failure modes: contrast-enhanced echocardiograms and poor-quality apical-4-chamber views. Selective estimation using intermediate features from EchoNet achieved the best performance across both estimation models (area under risk-coverage curve, EchoNet: 5.04 [4.45, 5.66]; PanEcho: 5.21 [4.54, 5.92]). CONCLUSIONS: Deep feature representations can be leveraged to identify and automatically flag misinterpretation-prone echocardiograms, enabling promising guardrail mechanisms for the reliable deployment of echocardiography AI.

title: Intravascular Imaging-Guided Drug-Eluting Stenting for Complex Coronary Lesions: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Intravascular imaging (IVI) guidance improves percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) outcomes, yet recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) challenged these findings. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of IVI-guided vs angiography-guided PCI in complex coronary lesions, incorporating recent large-scale trials with divergent findings. METHODS: The authors conducted a meta-analysis of RCTs evaluating IVI-guided vs angiography-guided PCI among patients with complex coronary lesions. The primary outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and cardiac death. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using frequentist random-effects models and complementary Bayesian analyses. The analysis was complemented by several sensitivity and subgroup analyses. RESULTS: Eighteen RCTs enrolling 18,975 patients were included. IVI guidance was associated with significant reductions in MACE (RR: 0.67; 95% CI: 0.55-0.83), cardiac death (RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.53-0.97), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.76-0.998), clinically driven target lesion revascularization (RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.51-0.999), and stent thrombosis (RR: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.35-0.78). A significant geographic interaction was identified for MACE, with benefit predominantly driven by Asian trial populations (Pinteraction < 0.01). In subgroup analysis, patients achieving imaging-defined stent optimization were associated with lower event rates than those who did not (RR: 0.41; 95% CI: 0.26-0.62). CONCLUSIONS: IVI guidance reduces the risk of adverse events for complex lesions. The benefit was in part driven by achieving imaging-defined stent optimization.

title: Left Ventricular Filling Pressure Classification by Electrocardiogram, Echocardiography, and Catheterization: Prognostic Implications.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Left ventricular diastolic filling pressure (LVFP) is a hallmark of heart failure. Although pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) measured during right heart catheterization (RHC) is the reference standard, echocardiography is more commonly used in practice. OBJECTIVES: The authors previously developed an artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiographic (AI-ECG) algorithm, trained on echocardiographic assessment, to classify LVFP. The aim of this study was to evaluate the prognostic implications of LVFP classification by AI-ECG, echocardiography, and PAWP among patients undergoing temporally proximate testing. METHODS: Adults who underwent echocardiography with electrocardiography within 14 days and RHC within 30 days were included. Elevated LVFP was defined as PAWP ≥15 mm Hg, grade 2 or 3 diastolic dysfunction by echocardiography, or elevated LVFP as classified by AI-ECG. Associations with all-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events were assessed. RESULTS: Among 4,168 patients (median age: 64 years; 47.7% women), elevated LVFP was classified by AI-ECG in 2,383 patients, by echocardiography in 1,643, and by PAWP in 1,841. AI-ECG showed good discrimination for echocardiographic LVFP (AUC: 0.879; 95% CI: 0.867-0.891) and moderate discrimination for PAWP (AUC: 0.711; 95% CI: 0.695-0.727). Over 7.7 years, 1,433 deaths occurred. Elevated LVFP classification by AI-ECG (adjusted HR [aHR]: 1.80; 95% CI: 1.55-2.09) and echocardiography (aHR: 1.74; 95% CI: 1.51-2.02) showed stronger associations with mortality than PAWP (aHR: 1.18; 95% CI: 1.05-1.31); in discordant cases, AI-ECG better predicted survival. Similar associations were observed for major adverse cardiovascular events. CONCLUSIONS: Despite moderate agreement with PAWP, echocardiography and AI-ECG showed stronger associations with clinical outcomes, suggesting they capture prognostically relevant myocardial information beyond resting hemodynamic status.

title: Mitral Valve Repair in Patients With Class I Obesity: A Propensity-Matched Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Obesity may increase the technical complexity of robotic mitral valve (MV) repair, but comparative outcomes with sternotomy remain poorly defined. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare perioperative and long-term outcomes of robotic vs sternotomy MV repair in patients with class I obesity. METHODS: A total of 880 patients with class I obesity (body mass index 30-34.9 kg/m2) underwent MV repair at our clinic between 2008 and 2025. After excluding those with mitral stenosis, active endocarditis, prior sternotomy, or concomitant procedures, 429 patients remained. Propensity score matching (1:1) yielded 132 patients in each group who underwent either robotic or conventional sternotomy MV repair. RESULTS: Median age was 59 years (IQR: 52-66), and 81% were male. Cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times were longer in the robotic group than in the sternotomy group (86 vs 65 minutes and 60 vs 48 minutes, respectively; P < 0.001). Robotic MV repair was associated with shorter hospitalization (3.5 vs 5 days; P < 0.001) and a lower postoperative transfusion rate (1.5% vs 10.6%; P = 0.002). There were no operative deaths in either group. No sternal wound infections occurred. Thirty-day readmission was numerically higher after robotic repair (12.8% vs 4.3%; P = 0.064). Ten-year survival was 92% (95% CI: 87% to 97%) with no significant difference between groups (P = 0.83). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with class I obesity, the robotic approach in comparison to sternotomy was associated with lower transfusion rates, shorter hospitalization, and comparable operative mortality and long-term survival relative to sternotomy. Although 30-day readmission was numerically higher among robotic patients, most events were minor and managed without intervention.

title: Effect of Colchicine on Arterial Stiffness in Patients With Hypertension: The COlchicine HypERtENsion Trial (COHERENT).
abstract: AIM: This trial investigated whether colchicine, an anti-inflammatory treatment, affects cardiovascular structure and function, assessed by arterial stiffness, blood pressure and biochemistry, compared with placebo. METHODS: COHERENT was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of the effects of colchicine on arterial stiffness in adults with pharmacologically treated hypertension without cardiovascular disease. Eligible patients were randomized 1:1 to colchicine 0.5mg daily or placebo for six months. Assessment of arterial stiffness, echocardiography, and biomarker measurement were performed at baseline and six months. The primary endpoint was change in carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV). Secondary endpoints included change in blood pressure (BP), left ventricular mass index, as well as change in cardiac and inflammatory biomarkers. RESULTS: Of 183 screened, 150 were randomized (75 per group). Mean age was 64.5 (±8.0) years, 53 (35.3%) were female, and mean systolic blood pressure was 137.6 (±15.6) mmHg. At six months, cfPWV did not differ between groups (between-group difference in ΔcfPWV -0.1m/s, 95% CI: -0.5 to 0.3m/s, p=0.53). Office systolic BP decreased significantly more in the placebo group than in the colchicine group (between-group difference in Δoffice systolic BP 5.7 mmHg, 95% CI: 1.0 to 10.5 mmHg, p=0.018. hsCRP decreased significantly in the colchicine group compared with the placebo group (between-group difference in % change in hsCRP -39.8%, 95% CI: -59.1 to -11.4%, p=0.010). Left ventricular mass index or cardiac biomarkers did not differ between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Six months of colchicine did not affect arterial stiffness in pharmacologically treated hypertension without cardiovascular disease. Colchicine significantly decreased hsCRP.

title: Intraoperative Dobutamine Plus Norepinephrine to Prevent Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Septic Shock: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: International guidelines recommend dobutamine for management of septic shock and cardiac dysfunction with persistent hypoperfusion in adults based on very low-certainty evidence. Randomized trials are lacking on the effect of intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine on postoperative outcomes in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduces acute kidney injury (AKI) within 7 postoperative days in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This randomized, open-label clinical trial in 39 tertiary hospitals in China enrolled adults with septic shock who were undergoing surgical source control between June 2024 and August 2025. Follow-up ended on November 15, 2025. INTERVENTION: Intraoperative, intravenous infusion of dobutamine (up to 5 µg/kg/min) combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine alone.
