MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was new-onset AKI or worsening of preoperative AKI within 7 days after surgery, defined using Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. The 11 secondary outcomes included Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score on postoperative day 1 and urine output 1 hour post intervention. RESULTS: Among 584 patients (median [IQR] age, 67.5 [55.0-76.0] years; 192 [32.9%] females), new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days occurred in 22.8% (66/290) randomized to receive dobutamine plus norepinephrine vs 34.7% (102/294) randomized to receive norepinephrine alone (adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 0.64 [95% CI, 0.49-0.83]). No significant differences were observed in 9 of the 11 secondary outcomes. SOFA scores on postoperative day 1 (adjusted difference, -0.53 [95% CI, -0.98 to -0.07]) were lower and urine output 1 hour post intervention (adjusted difference, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.03 to 1.07] mL/kg/h) was higher in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group. Stage 2 and 3 AKI were lower in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group compared with the norepinephrine alone group (stage 2: 4.8% vs 9.9%; ARR, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.26-0.88]; stage 3: 7.9% vs 13.6%; ARR, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.35-0.91]). Tachycardia (heart rate >100/min) occurred more frequently in patients receiving dobutamine and norepinephrine than norepinephrine alone. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among adult patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control, intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduced the incidence of new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days compared with norepinephrine. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06462313.

title: Coexistance of Carotid Sinus Hypersensitivity and Orthostatic Hypotension in Patients with Unexplained Syncope.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Carotid sinus hypersensitivity (CSH) and orthostatic hypotension (OH) are established causes of syncope but are often considered separate entities. However, evidence suggests that CSH and OH may coexist and jointly contribute to syncope. This study investigates the relationship between CSH and OH in patients with unexplained syncope. METHODS: A total of 1,908 patients aged ≥40 years (age, 63.7 ± 13.0 years; men, 45.3%) with unexplained syncope underwent carotid sinus massage (CSM) and head-up tilt testing (HUT). Occurrence of CSH in classical and delayed OH, including asystolic CSM responses was analysed. RESULTS: Six-hundred-and-eighteen patients (32.4%, 68.9 ± 11.3 years) had OH, while CSH was present in 320 patients (16.8%, 72.2 ± 9.9 years), and was more common in patients with OH than without OH (24.1% vs. 13.3%, p < 0.001). Among patients with CSH, 46.6% also had OH. CSH occurred equally in both classical OH (62/275, 22.5%) and delayed OH (87/345, 25.2%). Among OH patients, CSH was associated with older age, male sex, lower supine diastolic blood pressure, hypertension, and syncope-related hospital admission. An asystolic CSM response was observed more often in OH patients (n = 42; 6.8%) compared with non-OH patients (n = 44, 3.4%, p < 0.001) and was associated with older age and lower resting heart rate. CONCLUSIONS: CSH and OH frequently coexist in adults over 40 years evaluated for syncope. CSM may reveal a clinically relevant cardioinhibitory reflex in a subgroup of OH patients, supporting comprehensive cardiovascular autonomic testing in unexplained syncope.

title: Temporal Dynamics of Complement Activation and Outcome in Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Immune-mediated inflammatory responses exacerbate brain injury and affect the prognosis in acute ischemic stroke. METHODS: We characterized longitudinal complement activation after acute ischemic stroke using serial plasma samples from 10 patients and 8 controls. Initial markers of classical (C1q), lectin (mannose-binding lectin), and alternative (complement factor Bb) pathways, as well as regulatory (complement factor H) and downstream markers (C3a, C5a, and C5b-9) were measured by ELISA at 9 time points. RESULTS: Patients with stroke showed broad complement activation, with increased C1q, mannose-binding lectin, complement factor Bb, C3a, C5a, and C5b-9, and reduced complement factor H compared with controls. Complement components showed distinct temporal patterns during follow-up. Complement factor Bb levels were lower in patients with unfavorable functional outcome and in those with moderate-to-severe stroke. C1q and C3a trajectories differed according to functional outcome, whereas C3a trajectories also differed according to stroke severity. C1q trajectories differed according to age group and infarct volume. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest dynamic, pathway-specific complement activation after acute ischemic stroke and highlight the need for larger studies to clarify its prognostic and therapeutic relevance.

title: Calcium Density as a Marker of Coronary Plaque Stabilization in Primary Prevention: The CAUGHT-CAD Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite primary prevention statin treatment, a substantial proportion of individuals remain at residual risk for cardiovascular events. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CTA) enables the quantification of compositional changes in calcified plaque. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to examine whether increases in coronary calcified plaque volume and density associated with statin therapy could be used as a marker of plaque stabilization in asymptomatic individuals undergoing serial coronary CTA. METHODS: In the CAUGHT-CAD trial, asymptomatic, statin-naive, intermediate-risk individuals were randomized to a primary prevention strategy (including statin treatment) vs usual care. Participants underwent coronary CTA at baseline and 3 years. In this post hoc analysis, volumes of 5 plaque subtypes were quantified: noncalcified (≤350 HU), low-density calcium (351-500 HU), intermediate-density calcium (501-700 HU), high-density calcium (701-1000 HU), and very high density calcium (>1,000 HU). The primary outcome was the per-lesion level change in volumes of calcified plaque subtypes. RESULTS: Eight hundred forty lesions were included from 338 participants (mean age: 58.3 ± 6.9 years, 57.1% men, 161 [47.6%] statin treated). Statin treatment was associated with greater progression in intermediate-density (β = 0.89, SE = 0.39; P = 0.02) and high-density (β = 0.79, SE = 0.24; P = 0.001) calcium, alongside regression of noncalcified plaque (β = -9.83, SE = 1.64; P < 0.001), following adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) level, and baseline plaque volume. Among statin-treated participants, LDL-C reduction ≥30% was associated with greater progression of high-density (β = 1.11, SE = 0.49; P = 0.03) and very high density (β = 1.68, SE = 0.85; P = 0.04) calcium. CONCLUSIONS: In asymptomatic, intermediate-risk individuals, statin treatment was associated with a shift toward higher density calcium within coronary plaques, most marked with effective lowering of LDL-C. (Coronary Artery Calcium Score: Use to Guide Management of Hereditary Coronary Artery Disease [CAUGHT-CAD]; ACTRN12614001294640).

title: Exercise Prescriptions for Cardiovascular Health in Adults: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement: A Report of the American College of Cardiology.
abstract: Regular physical activity and structured exercise are foundational for cardiovascular prevention and treatment, yet exercise prescription remains inconsistently integrated into routine cardiovascular care. This American College of Cardiology scientific statement provides contemporary, practical guidance for clinicians on prescribing exercise across the spectrum of cardiovascular health and disease. The statement reviews evidence supporting physical activity, exercise training, and cardiorespiratory fitness as powerful determinants of cardiovascular outcomes, emphasizing that the greatest absolute benefits occur when inactive individuals begin moving and that additional benefits accrue with higher volumes and intensity, within appropriate clinical limits. It summarizes approaches to aerobic, resistance, balance, and flexibility training; highlights the role of cardiac rehabilitation and supervised, home-based, hybrid, and virtual models; and addresses individualized exercise prescription for patients with coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, heart failure, cardiomyopathies, hypertension, overweight and obesity, adult congenital heart disease, and older age. The statement also discusses when exercise testing is useful to assess safety, guide intensity, establish baseline fitness, and monitor responses, while recognizing that routine preparticipation testing is not required for most asymptomatic individuals. Wearable devices and digital tools are reviewed as adjuncts to self-monitoring, goal setting, and cardiac rehabilitation extension, with attention to equity, access, and digital literacy. Key implementation priorities include improving clinician training, embedding physical activity counseling into cardiovascular care, tailoring prescriptions to patient goals and functional capacity, and expanding research on long-term adherence, clinical outcomes, diverse populations, and scalable delivery models. Exercise should be prescribed as a core component of cardiovascular prevention and disease management.

title: Adult Attention Deficit-Hyperactivity Disorder.
abstract: Attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a medical condition that is present in approximately 2.5% of adults worldwide and manifests in a variety of different ways across the lifespan. Adults with ADHD often have coexisting psychiatric disorders such as anxiety, mood, sleep, substance use, and personality disorders and are at increased risk for coexisting somatic conditions such as obesity, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, type 1 and type 2 diabetes, and immune and inflammatory conditions. Hence, such adults may be seen by clinicians providing care for a wide range of psychiatric and somatic conditions. Nevertheless, ADHD remains unrecognized and undiagnosed in many persons. Assessment requires interviewing of the patient for core ADHD symptoms, coexisting conditions, and their functional effects, which can be facilitated by using standardized rating scales. Key components of treatment are psychoeducation and psychostimulant or nonstimulant medication, mostly in combination with psychosocial interventions and lifestyle guidance.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of NT-proBNP thresholds in Dyspneic Patients in the Emergency Department according to patients' characteristics: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Concentrations of N-terminal pro-B type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is central to acute heart failure (AHF) diagnosis in dyspneic emergency departments (ED) patients, but optimal thresholds remain uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of various NT-proBNP thresholds for AHF, across the general population and these key subgroups. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted, including studies published up to August 28, 2025, that reported the diagnostic performance of NT-proBNP thresholds for AHF in dyspneic ED patients. RESULTS: The analysis included 31 studies comprising 26,948 patients. To exclude AHF, a fixed threshold of ≤300 ng/L yielded an area under the receiver operator characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.73 (0.69-0.77), with high sensitivity of 97.9% (96.9-98.5) and lower specificity of 46.2% (36.4-56.2); the negative predictive value of this threshold was 97.0% (96.5-97.4). Age-dependent thresholds (≥450 ng/L for patients aged <50 years, ≥900 ng/L for those aged 50-75 years, and ≥1,800 ng/L for those aged ≥75 years), evaluated in 14,410 patients, achieved an AUC of 0.84 (0.83-0.85) with a more favorable balance between sensitivity of 85.9% (85.0-86.7) and specificity of 82.0% (81.2-82.9). In patients with CKD (N=2,271), all fixed thresholds yielded AUC <0.80; age-dependent thresholds showed an AUC of 0.77 (0.75-0.78) with specificity of 62.6% (59.4-65.7). In patients with obesity (body mass index ≥30), only age-dependent thresholds were assessed, in 3,562 patients; AUC was 0.82 (0.81-0.84) and sensitivity was 81.2% (79.2-83.1), broadly comparable to the overall population. CONCLUSION: A threshold ≤300 ng/L provides excellent rule-out performance for AHF, while age-dependent NT-proBNP thresholds offer superior diagnostic performance for ruling in AHF in the ED compared to fixed thresholds, and demonstrate consistent accuracy across subgroups. However, evidence in patients with CKD and obesity remains limited, both in terms of sample size and the range of thresholds evaluated.

title: Joint Impacts of Ambient Air Pollution and Temperature on Cardiovascular Disease in West Florida.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ambient temperature and fine particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter ≤2.5 μm (PM2.5) are well-established contributors of acute cardiovascular events, but their joint short-term effects in subtropical coastal regions have not been well characterized. We evaluated their joint associations with major cardiovascular outcomes in West Florida. METHODS: We analyzed daily hospital admissions for myocardial infarction, heart failure, and stroke within the BayCare Health System from 2017 to 2024. Daily mean temperature and PM2.5 were obtained from national monitoring networks. Joint exposure-response relationships were estimated using distributed-lag generalized additive models with tensor-product interactions across lags 0 to 7 days, adjusting for temporal trends, day of week, and copollutants. Effect modification by age, sex, and race was examined. RESULTS: Temperature showed stronger short-term associations with cardiovascular risk than local PM2.5. Among adults aged ≥65 years, myocardial infarction risk was higher at lower temperatures, compared with higher temperatures (relative risk comparing the 75th versus the 25th percentile of the exposure distribution [RR75/25], 0.92 [95% CI, 0.89-0.95]). Heart failure exhibited a U-shaped temperature-risk relationship, with greater heat-related risk observed among younger adults (RR75/25, 1.05 [95% CI, 1.02-1.09]) and Black patients (RR75/25, 1.05 [95% CI, 1.02-1.09]). In contrast, PM2.5 showed weaker overall associations, with only a modest elevation in stroke risk among Black patients (RR75/25, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.96-1.08]). Joint exposure surfaces revealed outcome-specific nonlinear patterns, particularly for heart failure at higher temperature and PM2.5. CONCLUSIONS: Temperature and PM2.5 jointly influence short-term cardiovascular risk through nonlinear and subgroup-specific pathways, highlighting the need for integrated climate and air-quality strategies to reduce cardiovascular disparities.

title: Lipoprotein(a) in Disaggregated South Asian Groups: An Analysis of MASALA and the UK Biobank.
abstract: BACKGROUND: South Asian individuals have a high prevalence of elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)], but little is known about the variation between disaggregated South Asian subgroups. OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to evaluate Lp(a) levels, nongenetic influences, and the association with incident atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) in South Asian populations using data from the Meditators of Atherosclerosis in South Asians Living in America (MASALA) and the UK Biobank (UKB) studies. METHODS: Lp(a) levels were assessed by South Asian country of origin and by state among Indian-origin participants. The association between nongenetic factors and Lp(a) levels was evaluated in multivariable linear regression models. Cox proportional hazards models evaluated the association between Lp(a) and ASCVD events in UKB participants. RESULTS: Among 2,074 MASALA participants born in the South Asian subcontinent (mean age: 56.7 ± 9.6 years), median [Q1-Q3] Lp(a) was 20.7 [10.5-43.0] mg/dL with significant variation by country of origin (P = 0.035). Median Lp(a) was 23 [11-48], 19 [10-37], 22 [11-47], and 17 [10-34] mg/dL in participants from Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka, respectively. Vegetarian diet, statin use, postmenopausal status, and fewer years in the United States were associated with higher Lp(a) levels while alcohol consumption was associated with lower Lp(a) levels. However, these associations were all very modest. Among 6,845 UKB participants (mean age: 55.1 ± 8.7 years; median Lp(a): 31 [13-65] nmol/L), the associations between Lp(a) and ASCVD did not vary by country of origin or South Asian ethnicity (P interaction > 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: There is modest variation in Lp(a) levels, but no difference in the association between Lp(a) and ASCVD outcomes, across South Asian subgroups.

title: Risk-weighted apoB and lipoprotein-associated coronary risk across ethnic groups.
abstract: AIMS: Apolipoprotein B (apoB) reflects the number of circulating atherogenic lipoproteins but does not account for differences in particle atherogenicity. Risk-weighted apoB (RW-apoB), which incorporates triglyceride-rich lipoproteins and lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)), may better capture lipoprotein-driven coronary risk, but its performance across diverse populations remains uncertain. We assessed whether the prespecified triglyceride - and Lp(a)-weighted information captured by RW-apoB was associated with coronary events beyond apoB and compared the discrimination of RW-apoB and measured apoB across ethnicities. METHODS: We analyzed 40,132 participants with 4,509 coronary events from ARIC, CARDIA, MESA, the Framingham Offspring Study, and China Kadoorie Biobank. RW-apoB was calculated using a prespecified equation. Mutually adjusted Cox estimates were pooled within ethnic groups using random-effects meta-analysis. Separate single-marker models compared discrimination. Sensitivity analyses included age and sex adjustment, standardized exposures, hard-events, truncated follow-up, and CKB-specific logistic regression. RESULTS: Mean RW-apoB exceeded apoB by approximately 8 mg/dL in African American and Chinese participants, reflecting higher lipoprotein(a) and triglycerides, respectively. RW-apoB was associated with coronary events conditional on apoB in White, African American, Chinese, and Hispanic participants: hazard ratios per 10 mg/dL were 1.11 (95% CI 1.05-1.18), 1.11 (1.08-1.15), 1.08 (1.05-1.11), and 1.10 (1.01-1.21), respectively. C-indices for RW-apoB versus apoB were 0.630 versus 0.617 in White (P<0.001), 0.606 versus 0.595 in African American (P=0.085), 0.567 versus 0.554 in Chinese (P=0.014), and 0.540 versus 0.535 in Hispanic participants (P=0.756). CONCLUSION: RW-apoB captured lipoprotein-associated risk beyond measured apoB, with discrimination gains statistically demonstrable in the larger White and Chinese groups.

title: Effectiveness of Discrete Strategies and Implementation Bundles for Improving Clinician Prescription of Clinical Practice Guideline-Recommended Medications for Atherosclerotic Occlusive Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: We sought to determine the effectiveness of discrete strategies and implementation bundles for improving clinical practice guideline (CPG) strongly recommended medication prescription to adults with atherosclerotic occlusive disease. METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, PsycINFO, and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (inception to December 9, 2025) for randomized controlled trials evaluating discrete strategies or implementation bundles for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription to adults with atherosclerotic occlusive disease. Two investigators screened titles/abstracts and full texts, extracted data, assessed risk of bias, and classified discrete strategies and implementation bundles. Random-effects models were used for meta-analysis. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation was used to assess certainty. RESULTS: We included 31 randomized controlled trials studying 29 unique discrete strategies and implementation bundles. The implementation bundle with the largest effect size for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription combined case management, team changes, continuous quality improvement, audit/feedback, and clinician and patient education (relative risk, 2.62 [95% CI, 2.08-3.29]; moderate certainty). Meta-regression analyses suggested that discrete strategies and implementation bundles using patient education were more effective at improving statin (P=0.037) and all CPG strongly recommended medication (P=0.006) prescription. Combining case management, team changes, facilitated relay of information, and audit/feedback reduced all-cause death and new vascular event risk. Team changes improved prescription of all CPG strongly recommended medications (relative risk, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.11-1.36]; moderate certainty) and reduced major adverse cardiac event risk. CONCLUSIONS: Combining case management, team changes, continuous quality improvement, audit/feedback, and clinician and patient education had the largest effect size for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription and improved patient outcomes. Team changes improved CPG strongly recommended medication prescription and reduced major adverse cardiac event risk.

title: Steatotic liver disease phenotypes and stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation: A nationwide population-based cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The updated nomenclature of steatotic liver disease (SLD) recognizes distinct phenotypes, including Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), MASLD with increased alcohol intake (MetALD), and alcohol-related liver disease (ALD). Although cardiovascular risk may differ across SLD phenotypes, their association with stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the association between SLD phenotypes and ischemic stroke risk in AF patients. METHODS: AF patients diagnosed between 2010 and 2018 were identified from the Korean health insurance database. According to SLD phenotype, patients were categorized into No-SLD, MASLD, MetALD, and ALD. The primary outcome was ischemic stroke. Subgroup analyses were conducted by CHA2DS2-VA score. RESULTS: Among 196,242 patients (No-SLD: 101,308; MASLD: 77,715; MetALD: 8,678; ALD: 8,541), median follow-up was 5.9 years. Compared with No-SLD, MASLD was not associated with stroke risk (adjusted hazard ratio and 95% confidence interval; 1.00, 0.97-1.04), whereas MetALD and ALD were associated with higher risk (1.09, 1.00-1.18 and 1.16, 1.08-1.26, respectively). In exploratory subgroup analyses, the higher risk associated with alcohol-related phenotypes appeared more apparent at lower CHA2DS2-VA scores; however, the 6-year absolute risk differences were approximately 1% or less, and these findings are regarded as hypothesis-generating. CONCLUSION: In patients with AF, stroke risk was significantly higher in the alcohol-related SLD phenotypes, MetALD and ALD, whereas MASLD was not associated with stroke risk. These findings are consistent with the current recommendations for comprehensive risk-factor management in AF, with particular attention to alcohol intake in patients with alcohol-related SLD phenotypes.

title: Global Prevalence of Adherence to Antihypertensives and Associated Moderating Factors Among Adults With Hypertension: A Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a significant public health issue affecting over a billion adults worldwide with adherence to antihypertensives being crucial for achieving sustained blood pressure control and reducing cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. To extend previous evidence, we conducted a meta-analysis on global prevalence of adherence to antihypertensives among adults. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and CINAHL. Pooled prevalence of antihypertensive medication adherence was estimated using generalized linear mixed-effects model in R software version 4.4.3. Cochran's Q, τ2, and I2$$ {I}^2 $$ statistics examined statistical heterogeneity with moderator analysis exploring sources of heterogeneity. Sensitivity analysis was analyzed using exact fixed-effects model. RESULTS: A total of 123 studies with 1 052 445 adults with hypertension were included. Pooled global prevalence of adherence to antihypertensives was estimated at 58% (95% CI, 52%-63%), with 39% for high adherence, 29% for moderate adherence, and 35% for low adherence. Results for sensitivity analysis were 57.91% (95% CI, 57.81%-58.01%) with δ̂ being 24.3%. Prevalence across continents was 67% for Europe, 65% for South America, 60% for Africa, 56% for Asia, and 45% for North America. Adherence to antihypertensives was similar across low-income countries (61%), high-income countries (58), upper-middle-income countries (57%), and lower-middle-income countries (56%). In multivariate model, age and assessment tool only were significantly associated with medication adherence. CONCLUSIONS: Globally, a large proportion of adults with hypertension exhibit moderate to low adherence to antihypertensive medications. Future studies should prioritize establishing consensus-based operational definitions and cutoff values to enhance adherence.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy for Secondary Stroke Prevention in Patients With Symptomatic Large-Artery Atherosclerosis and Atrial Fibrillation: A Multicenter Experience.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Optimal antithrombotic therapy for ischemic stroke due to symptomatic large-artery atherosclerosis in patients with atrial fibrillation remains uncertain. We describe real-world prescribing patterns and outcomes across antithrombotic regimens. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with atrial fibrillation and ischemic stroke related to symptomatic large-artery atherosclerosis (intracranial or extracranial or both) at 4 US comprehensive stroke centers. Patients were grouped by discharge regimen: single anticoagulant, single antiplatelet (sAP), single anticoagulant+sAP, dual antiplatelet therapy, or triple therapy (single anticoagulant+dual antiplatelet therapy). Outcomes were recurrent ischemic stroke, symptomatic hemorrhage, and death at 90 days and 1 year. RESULTS: Among 191 patients (median age 75 years [interquartile range [IQR], 68-83]; 40% women; 36% prior stroke/transient ischemic attack), single anticoagulant+sAP was the most common discharge regimen (33%), followed by single anticoagulant (25%), whereas triple therapy was uncommon (4%). More than half of patients switched regimens within 1 year, mostly as the planned duration ended (71%) or following an outcome event (12%). During follow-up (median 68 days [IQR, 28-120]), 21 patients (11%) had recurrent ischemic stroke, and 26 (14%) had symptomatic hemorrhage, over half of each within 90 days; 25% of deaths occurred within 90 days. Ninety-day stroke/death rate was 24%, with single anticoagulant versus 8% with single anticoagulant+sAP; symptomatic hemorrhage rate was 0% and 12%, respectively. At 1 year, stroke/death was 27.3% with sAP, 11.1% with single anticoagulant+sAP, 4.5% with single anticoagulant, and 0% with dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic hemorrhage was similar across groups. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with atrial fibrillation and symptomatic large-artery atherosclerosis, recurrent ischemic events and mortality were common, and antithrombotic management varied substantially. The combination of single anticoagulant+sAP was associated with lower observed short-term stroke/death than single anticoagulant; however, bleeding remains a concern with prolonged therapy. Prospective studies are needed to define optimal regimen and duration for this high-risk population.

title: Mental Health Factors in Cardiothoracic Surgery Risk Prediction Models: A Systematic Review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mental health disorders are associated with substantial morbidity and death in cardiovascular disease, yet their role in perioperative risk stratification remains unclear in patients undergoing cardiothoracic surgery. We evaluated how mental health disorders are currently incorporated into cardiothoracic surgery risk prediction models. METHODS: We conducted a Preferred Reporting Items for Systemic Reviews and Meta-Analysis-concordant systematic review of PubMed and Embase on September 11, 2025 (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews: CRD420251274958). We included studies that developed or validated risk models predicting postoperative outcomes in adults undergoing cardiothoracic surgery that either included a mental health disorder as a covariate or validated a model in patients with such disorders. Model characteristics were extracted using the Checklist for Critical Appraisal and Data Extraction for Systemic Reviews of Prediction Modeling Studies, and risk of bias and applicability were assessed using the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool+Artificial Intelligence. Findings were synthesized qualitatively. RESULTS: Of 17 986 articles screened, 9 studies met inclusion criteria and described 17 unique models. No study validated a model specifically in patients with mental health disorders. Depression was the most frequently included mental health covariate (8 models). When incorporated, mental health disorders had associations comparable to established clinical risk factors. The most frequently modeled outcomes were hospital readmission and postoperative depression. Three studies had a high risk of bias. Covariate selection and modeled outcomes varied substantially. CONCLUSIONS: Mental health disorders are rarely incorporated into cardiothoracic surgery risk models despite potentially important prognostic associations. Future studies should evaluate their incremental predictive value, validate models in patients with mental health disorders, and examine intersections with sociodemographic risk factors.

title: Associations of Physical Activity and Diet Quality With Mortality and Cardiovascular Disease in Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Physical activity (PA) and diet are cornerstones for cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention, yet their associations with CVD within the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework remain unexplored. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the independent and joint associations of PA and/or diet quality with mortality and incident CVD across CKM stages. METHODS: Our study included 339,074 UK Biobank participants (51.3% women, mean age 56.4 years) with CKM syndrome stage 0 to 4. PA was categorized as high (≥150 min/wk of walking or moderate-to-vigorous activity) or low using self-reported and accelerometer-measured data. Diet quality was classified as low/median/high. Cox proportional hazards models assessed associations with incident CVD, cause-specific CVD mortality, and all-cause mortality across CKM stages. RESULTS: High PA was associated with lower risks of all-cause mortality (HR: 0.76 [95% CI: 0.74-0.79]), composite CVD mortality (0.74 [0.70-0.77]), and incident composite CVD (0.90 [0.88-0.92]); for high diet quality, corresponding HRs (95% CIs) were 0.81 (0.77-0.85), 0.81 (0.75-0.88), and 0.87 (0.84-0.90). PA showed nonlinear associations with these outcomes, plateauing at approximately 2,500 metabolic equivalent min/wk. High PA combined with high diet quality showed stronger inverse associations with all-cause mortality (0.64 [0.60-0.68]), composite CVD mortality (0.61 [0.54-0.68]), and incident composite CVD (0.83 [0.79-0.88]). Significant multiplicative interactions between PA and diet quality were observed for stroke mortality, composite CVD, and heart failure. The joint associations with these outcomes were stronger at more advanced CKM syndrome stages. CONCLUSIONS: Beyond individual benefits, joint PA-diet modification was associated with lower risk of mortality and CVD across CKM stages, highlighting the value of integrated behavioral strategies.

title: Evaluating the Role of Lower Extremity Elastic Bandage in Patients with Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lower extremity compression therapy has been proposed as an adjunct to mitigate diuretic resistance during acute decompensation of heart failure (ADHF). We evaluated the effect of lower leg compression with elastic bandages on diuretic efficiency in patients with diuretic-resistant ADHF. METHODS: Historical cohort study enrolling adult cardiac ICU admissions with ADHF who used elastic bandages (EB) at Mayo Clinic in Minnesota from 2007 to 2017. The diuretic efficiency before and after applying EB was the primary outcome. RESULTS: A total of 176 patients with heart failure who received elastic bandages were included. The in-hospital mortality rate, the median hospital length of stay, and 30-day hospital readmission were 9.7%, 11.4 days (IQR 7.1-19.0), and 11%, respectively. When EB was applied, the average daily loop diuretic dosage was decreased by a mean difference of 1.19 mg per 40 mg furosemide equivalent (95% CI: 0.22 to 2.2; p = 0.016). The average post-EB diuretic efficiency was 1,355 mL (IQR 1,119, 1,590) per 40-mg furosemide, which was significantly higher than before EB application, with a mean difference of 340 mL per 40-mg furosemide equivalent (95% CI: -554, -125; p = 0.002). A higher diuretic efficiency led to lower diuretic doses. Average daily urine output before and after EB application was not different (2,642 pre-EB vs. 2,792 post-EB mL/day; 95% CI: -455 to 154; p = 0.33). CONCLUSION: EB use enhances diuretic efficacy during ADHF. Further studies are needed to determine the potential clinical benefits and risks of applying EB compression treatment in ADHF.

title: Stroke Risk-Based Anticoagulation After Atrial Fibrillation Ablation: ALONE-AF Post-Hoc Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Discontinuation of oral anticoagulant (OAC) in patients without recurrent atrial arrhythmia after ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF) has been demonstrated to reduce composite outcomes of stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding compared with continued OAC. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the optimal OAC strategy according to baseline stroke risk and AF recurrence. METHODS: In this post-hoc analysis of the Long-Term Anticoagulation Discontinuation after Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation (ALONE-AF) trial, patients were stratified according to CHA2DS2-VASc score ≤2 and ≥3. Within each stratum, outcomes were compared between the OAC discontinuation and continuation subgroups. The cumulative incidence of stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding at 2 years was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with competing risk analysis accounting for AF recurrence. RESULTS: Among 840 patients, 584 and 256 had a CHA2DS2-VASc score ≤2 (mean age 62.0±7.5 years, 15.9% female) and ≥3 (mean age 68.9±7.3 years, 45.3% female), respectively. In the CHA2DS2-VASc ≤2 stratum, the primary outcome occurred in one patient (0.4%) in discontinuation subgroup vs. six (2.4%) in continuation subgroup (absolute difference -1.9 percentage points, P=0.066). In the CHA2DS2-VASc ≥3 stratum, two events (1.8%) occurred in the continuation subgroup only (absolute difference -1.8 percentage points, P=0.172). All major bleeding events (n=5) occurred in the continuation subgroups. Competing risk analysis yielded consistent results. CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory post-hoc analysis, no statistically significant differences in outcomes were observed between OAC strategies when stratified by CHA2DS2-VASc score, though event numbers were limited. Larger prospective trials are needed to confirm these observations. TRIAL REGISTRATIONS: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04432220.

title: Unipolar Electrograms at the Pulmonary Vein Antrum: Spatial and Directional Heterogeneity with Distinct Postablation Morphologies.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Disappearance of the near-field S-wave in the unipolar electrogram (U-EGM) is commonly used to assess lesion formation during pulmonary vein (PV) isolation; however, interpretation of U-EGMs in anatomically complex atrial regions remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: We aimed to characterize spatial, directional, and postablation changes in antral PV U-EGMs, and evaluate the limitations of conventional waveform interpretation. METHODS: In 15 patients undergoing radiofrequency ablation for atrial fibrillation, U-EGMs were recorded at 116 antral PV sites during sinus rhythm and distal coronary sinus (CS) pacing before and after ablation. U-EGM morphology and R- and S-wave amplitudes were analyzed. RESULTS: Baseline U-EGMs showed spatial heterogeneity, with a small r and deep S in the right anterior PV antrum transitioning to a positive-dominant morphology (Rs) in the left-lower PV antra. Distal CS pacing altered the activation sequence, causing direction-dependent changes, most prominently in the right PV antrum. After ablation, overall S-wave amplitude decreased from -0.94 ± 0.70 to -0.08 ± 0.55 mV (P<0.001). Residual negative deflections ≥0.5 mV persisted in 18.1% (21/116) of recordings, frequently in association with direction-dependent far-field activity. Newly developed positive deflections ≥1.0 mV were observed in 17/116 sites (14.7%; mean 1.42 ± 0.42 mV), predominantly in the right-sided antra. CONCLUSIONS: Antral PV U-EGMs frequently represent composites of near- and far-field signals with spatial heterogeneity and direction-dependent variation. Postablation responses are diverse, including S-wave disappearance, residual negativity, often reflecting contributions from overlapping far-field components, and newly developed positive deflections. PV-antral U-EGMs should be interpreted in the context of their composite nature.

title: Intermittent or Continuous Renal-Replacement Therapy in Acute Kidney Injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The preferred method of renal-replacement therapy for acute kidney injury in critically ill patients remains uncertain. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned critically ill adults with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy to undergo intermittent hemodialysis or continuous renal-replacement therapy as the initial treatment. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event - defined as death, dependence on renal-replacement therapy, or a serum creatinine concentration more than 25% above the baseline value - by day 90. RESULTS: The trial was stopped early after sequential interim analyses showed a sustained signal of higher mortality with intermittent hemodialysis than with continuous renal-replacement therapy. A total of 554 patients underwent randomization, with 272 patients assigned to undergo intermittent hemodialysis and 282 to undergo continuous renal-replacement therapy; 535 patients (260 in the intermittent group and 275 in the continuous group) were included in the intention-to-treat population. A major adverse kidney event occurred by day 90 in 203 patients (78.1%) in the intermittent group and in 197 patients (71.6%) in the continuous group (adjusted absolute risk difference, 6.28 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.22 to 13.79). Death by day 90 occurred in 164 patients (63.1%) and in 147 patients (53.5%), respectively. Kaplan-Meier mortality estimates at day 90 were 63.3% and 53.6% (hazard ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.63). The most common complication potentially related to acute kidney injury or renal-replacement therapy was hypotension, which occurred in 179 patients (68.8%) in the intermittent group and in 183 patients (66.5%) in the continuous group. CONCLUSIONS: Among critically ill patients with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy, intermittent hemodialysis as the initial treatment approach was not shown to be noninferior to continuous renal-replacement therapy with respect to major adverse kidney events by day 90 and was associated with higher mortality. (Funded by the French Ministry of Health; ICRAKI ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06032884.).

title: Association of Non-Cytochrome P450 3A4-Metabolized Statins Versus Atorvastatin With Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Cancer Receiving Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: A Propensity Score-Matched Target Trial Emulation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) often undergo CYP3A4 (cytochrome P450 3A4) metabolism. Atorvastatin is a CYP3A4 substrate, whereas rosuvastatin and pitavastatin largely bypass this pathway. We evaluated whether statin choice was associated with major adverse cardiovascular events in TKI-treated patients with cancer. METHODS: Using TriNetX, we conducted an active-comparator, new-user target trial emulation among adults with cancer receiving their first TKI. The index date was the first statin dispensation; outcome ascertainment began on Day 30 and continued up to 3 years. Separate 1:1 propensity score-matched comparisons included rosuvastatin versus atorvastatin (primary; 2215 per group), pitavastatin comparisons, and a pooled non-CYP3A4 statin comparison. RESULTS: Among 10 843 eligible patients (mean age, 66.7 years; 60.7% male), rosuvastatin was associated with a lower major adverse cardiovascular events rate than atorvastatin (624 versus 769 events; hazard ratio [HR], 0.84 [95% CI, 0.76-0.93]). The proportional-hazards assumption was violated (P=0.042), so the HR was interpreted as a time-averaged association. The pooled comparison was concordant (HR, 0.87 [95% CI, 0.78-0.96]). The early-persistence Day-180 estimate was imprecise (HR, 0.90 [95% CI, 0.73-1.09]). CONCLUSIONS: Rosuvastatin use was associated with lower major adverse cardiovascular events than atorvastatin in TKI-treated patients with cancer. This observational finding is compatible with, but does not establish, a CYP3A4-mediated interaction. Residual confounding, nonaligned TKI and statin timing in part of the primary cohort, and lack of individual-level event-time data require prospective confirmation.

title: Intraprocedural Cardiac Arrest in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Interventions in the United States: An Analysis of the NCDR CathPCI Registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiac arrest (CA) during percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) is a catastrophic procedural complication. Contemporary rates of CA during PCI are unknown. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to understand contemporary rates of CA, associated mortality, and identify predictors of CA during PCI. METHODS: Patients with CA during PCI from 2018 to 2023 were identified from the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI Registry. Trends in intraprocedural CA (IPCA) incidence and in-hospital death were evaluated. Predictors of IPCA and risk-adjusted mortality were identified. RESULTS: A total of 36,755 IPCA occurred during 3,956,840 PCIs (0.93%), including in 0.24% of elective PCIs, 0.32% of PCIs for stable coronary artery disease, and 1.28% of acute coronary syndrome interventions. The incidence of IPCA increased over time (0.62% in 2018 to 1.07% in 2023; P < 0.0001). In-hospital death occurred in 40.5% of patients with IPCA, 45.4% of whom died in the cardiac catheterization laboratory. Notably, although risk-adjusted IPCA increased (0.79% to 0.95%; P = 0.042), slight declines in risk-adjusted mortality (45.1% to 43.6%; P = 0.027) were observed over time. PCI for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, non-ST-segment acute coronary syndromes, increasing age, ventricular arrhythmias, severe aortic stenosis, vasopressors or inotrope use, mechanical circulatory support, coronary perforation, coronary dissection, cardiac tamponade, intraprocedural heart failure or myocardial infarction, and temporary cardiac pacemaker implantation were associated with increased adjusted odds of IPCA. CONCLUSIONS: IPCA complicates 0.93% of contemporary PCI. Despite an increasing incidence of risk-adjusted IPCA, there were slight declines in risk-adjusted in-hospital mortality in the study period. Several patient and procedural characteristics were independently associated with intraprocedural CA.

title: Latent class analysis-derived patterns of comorbidities in patients with atrial fibrillation, adherence to integrated care and impact on long-term outcomes: an analysis from a prospective cohort.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) commonly coexists with multiple cardiovascular (CV) and non-CV comorbidities, which may cluster in distinct clinical phenotypes with different outcome implications. OBJECTIVE: We aim to identify comorbidity-based phenotypes in AF using latent class analysis (LCA), characterize their clinical course and assess the association of integrated care adherence with outcomes across phenotypes. METHODS: A LCA based on 11 conditions (CV and non-CV) was performed. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, thromboembolic (TE) events, and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Secondary outcomes were all-cause death and ACS/TE events. RESULTS: We included 1233 AF patients (median age 75 [66-82] years, females 37.5%). Four clinical LCA-derived phenotypes were identified: "Low comorbidity" (31.5%); "Cardio-metabolic" (33.9%); "Elderly comorbid" (22.9%); and "Atherosclerotic-HF" (11.8%). During a median follow-up of 542 days, 234 patients (22.7%) experienced the primary outcome. Compared to "Low comorbidity", "Cardio-metabolic" (aHR 1.64, 95% CI 1.13-2.39), "Elderly comorbid" (aHR 1.62, 95% CI 1.09-2.42) and "Atherosclerotic-HF" (aHR 2.81, 95%CI 1.83-4.34) phenotypes were independently associated with a higher risk of the primary outcome. Adherence to integrated care varied across phenotypes and was associated with a lower risk of adverse events, with no evidence of significant heterogeneity across phenotypes (p int=0.157). CONCLUSIONS: Latent class analysis identified distinct AF clinical phenotypes characterized by specific patterns of comorbidities and associated with different risk of adverse outcomes. The absence of significant heterogeneity in the association between integrated care and outcomes across phenotypes supports its potential value across different levels of clinical complexity in AF patients.

title: Pulmonary Embolism-Attributable Mortality in Patients With Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease in the United States from 2010 to 2023.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) are at increased risk of pulmonary embolism (PE) and related mortality, yet contemporary US trends remain incompletely defined. We examined PE-attributable mortality from 2010 to 2023 among patients with ASCVD, stratified by age, sex, race, ethnicity, urbanization, and region. METHODS: We used the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Wide-Ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research data (2010-2023) to assess PE-attributable mortality among patients with ASCVD aged ≥15 years using age-adjusted mortality rates. Concurrent trends in age-adjusted ASCVD prevalence and risk factors were evaluated using NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey). Age-adjusted mortality rates were analyzed with Joinpoint regression to estimate average annual percentage change (95% CI), and trends in NHANES were assessed using linear models. RESULTS: From 2010 to 2023, 152 386 US patients with ASCVD aged ≥15 years (80 015 male, 72 371 female) died from PE. PE-attributable AAMR rose from 3.62 to 4.96 per 100 000 (annual percentage change +3.1%; P<0.001), with a modest increase from 2010 to 2018 (annual percentage change +0.7%, P=0.003) and a sharp rise from 2018 to 2023 (annual percentage change +12.8%, P<0.001). Age-adjusted mortality rate was highest in non-Hispanic/non-Latinx Black American individuals, and American Indian/Alaska Native and Hispanic/Latinx populations had the steepest increases. Adults <65 years, rural areas, and the Western United States showed disproportionate rises, whereas the South had the highest absolute deaths. Such trends paralleled increasing ASCVD prevalence, which was driven by hypertension, obesity, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease. CONCLUSIONS: PE-attributable mortality among US patients with ASCVD rose from 2010 to 2023 particularly among young-to-middle-aged adults, socioeconomically isolated ethnic and racial groups, and Western residents.

title: American Heart Association Life's Essential 8 and Heart Failure in Black Individuals: An Analysis of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Self-reported Black individuals have a disproportionately high prevalence of heart failure (HF) compared with other racial groups. In an effort to empower patients and health providers to combat cardiovascular disease, the American Heart Association identified Life's Essential 8 as the 8 health behaviors crucial for heart health. In this study, we evaluate the association between components of Life's Essential 8 and HF outcomes among Black individuals. METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study analyzed 107 622 individuals captured in the NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey) from 1999 to 2020 who were categorized by self-reported race. To represent Life's Essential 8, variables of self-reported sleep duration, physical activity, smoking status, and dietary habits were used. Additionally, self-reported diagnoses of diabetes, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and heart failure were included. Multivariable logistic regression models were constructed to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% CIs for the associations between Life's Essential 8 components and HF among Black individuals. RESULTS: Black individuals were diagnosed with HF at a younger age compared with White individuals (54 years vs 65 years, P<0.001). Among Black individuals, body mass index (odds ratio [OR], 1.041 [95% CI, 1.027-1.055], P=0.02), hypertension (OR, 3.175 [95% CI, 2.14-4.69], P<0.0001), hyperlipidemia (OR, 1.36 [95% CI, 1.04-1.76], P=0.02), and diabetes (OR, 2.07 [95% CI, 1.60-2.67], P≤0.0001) were associated with increased odds of HF. Physical activity was associated with lower odds (OR, 0.564 [95% CI, 0.38-0.836], P=0.004) of HF in Black individuals. CONCLUSIONS: Black individuals experienced HF at significantly younger ages, with traditional cardiometabolic factors (body mass index, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes) each independently being associated with HF risk. Physical activity appears protective, underscoring the importance of early, targeted prevention strategies.

title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Non-Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study. METHODS: In a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate. RESULTS: A total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; P<0.001). The mean percentage of time that the CGM-measured glucose level was in the glucose-level range of 70 to 180 mg per deciliter was 21 percentage points higher (95% CI, 16 to 26) with CGM than with routine care (P<0.001). The between-group difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 54 mg per deciliter was -0.17 percentage points (95% CI, -0.27 to -0.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 70 mg per deciliter was -0.20 percentage points (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.09; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.004 for superiority). No severe hypoglycemia events were reported. CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. title: Coronary artery disease management in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
abstract: Background: The optimal management of coronary artery disease in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain. Aims: We aimed to compare clinical outcomes between routine coronary revascularisation and conservative management in patients undergoing TAVI and to assess the relative effectiveness of individual revascularisation strategies by performing a meta-analysis of randomised trials. Methods: We conducted a pairwise meta-analysis comparing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with conservative treatment and a network meta-analysis comparing the relative effectiveness of individual strategies, including angiography-guided and physiology-guided PCI. The primary outcome was a study-defined composite endpoint of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary endpoints included the individual outcomes of all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, unplanned revascularisation, and major bleeding. Results: Five trials (N=1,644 patients) were included in the systematic review, and four were included in the primary quantitative synthesis (N=1,476). Compared with conservative treatment, routine PCI was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio [RR] 0.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.98) and unplanned revascularisation (RR 0.30, 95% CI: 0.11-0.83) and an increased risk of major bleeding (RR 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32). In the network meta-analysis, physiology-guided PCI significantly reduced MACE, stroke, and unplanned revascularisation compared with conservative treatment and ranked highest for all ischaemic outcomes among revascularisation strategies. Conclusions: Among patients referred for TAVI, routine revascularisation reduces the risk of ischaemic outcomes compared with conservative treatment. In this setting, physiology-guided PCI may be associated with the most favourable efficacy profile across available strategies.

title: Safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System in acute intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism: the SPIRARE II pivotal trial
abstract: Background: Percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy can rapidly reduce afterload in acute pulmonary embolism (PE), but catheter stiffness and instability may limit access and prevent effective right ventricle (RV) unloading. The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System with Transforming Fixation (TFX) technology is designed to address current limitations of existing catheter-based systems by separating the flexibility necessary for safe navigation from the support that is essential for procedural control. Aims: We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System for mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in acute intermediate-risk PE. Methods: SPIRARE II was a prospective, single-arm, multicentre pivotal investigation conducted at 19 sites in the United States and Europe. Eligible patients had acute PE (≤14 days), a computed tomography angiography-assessed RV to left ventricle (RV/LV) ratio>0.9, and haemodynamic stability (systolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg). Co-primary endpoints were composite major adverse events (MAE) within 48 hours and core laboratory-assessed RV/LV change from baseline to 48 hours. Prespecified secondary endpoints were collected immediately pre- and post-procedure in all patients including mean pulmonary artery pressure, total pulmonary vascular resistance, and cardiac index. Results: In 123 patients, the 48-hour composite MAE rate was 2.4% (3/123), meeting the prespecified performance goal (one-sided p<0.0001). The mean RV/LV diameter ratio decreased from 1.44±0.33 at baseline to 1.05±0.21 at 48 hours, a mean reduction of 0.39±0.33, exceeding the prespecified performance goal (p<0.0001). Conclusions: The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System met its prespecified safety and effectiveness endpoints in acute intermediate-risk PE. TFX delivered precise, stable control with reliable vessel access, enabling consistent right ventricular unloading.

title: Early outcomes of transcatheter vacuum-assisted mass extraction in the left heart and the aortic arch
abstract: Background: Transcatheter vacuum-assisted mass extraction (TVME) in the systemic circulation is increasingly being reported. However, its feasibility, effectiveness, and safety remain poorly defined. Aims: We sought to investigate the feasibility, effectiveness and safety of TVME in the left heart and aortic arch. Methods: Consecutive patients from 6 centres in the United States and Canada were included. Feasibility was defined as technically successful mass extraction without unplanned cardiac surgery or intraprocedural mortality. The effectiveness endpoint was feasibility with successful debulking of ≥70% mass volume. The primary safety endpoint was the 30-day composite of procedure-attributable mortality, major cardiac structural complications, major vascular complications, Type 3-4 bleeding, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and stroke, all according to Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3 definitions. Intraprocedural events were also reported. Results: A total of 62 consecutive patients were evaluated. Feasibility was reached in 85.5% of patients and effectiveness in 77.4% of patients – except for 11.3% with suboptimal debulking, 3.2% with access-related case abortion, and 8.1% with case cancellation where no mass was found intraprocedurally. The primary safety endpoint occurred in 14.5% of patients, with a procedure-attributable mortality rate of 3.2%. VARC-3 major cardiac structural complications, major vascular complications, Type 3-4 bleeding, ACS, and stroke occurred in 3.2%, 8.1%, 3.2%, 3.2%, and 6.5% of patients, respectively. Intraprocedural events included hypoxia (6.5%), hypotension (9.7%), embolism (3.2%), air embolism (1.6%), and increased mitral regurgitation (6.5%). Conclusions: TVME in left-sided and aortic arch masses is feasible and demonstrates reasonable effectiveness. However, the considerable rate of safety-related events highlights the need for better case selection and procedural refinement, such as optimal embolic protection.
